### DependencyInjection

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:35` · Level 10 · class (static, with one `extension(IServiceCollection)` block)

- **What it is**: the composition root of the UI layer. One `AddUIShared(configuration)` call wires the shared UI infrastructure every head needs (Blazor Server, WebAssembly, MAUI), and twelve smaller methods cover the per-head, per-module and per-opt-in registrations.
- **Depends on**: nearly the whole group. Settings: [ApiSettings](#apisettings) / [ApiSettingsValidator](#apisettingsvalidator), [LayoutSettings](#layoutsettings), [LegalSettings](#legalsettings), [RegistrationSettings](#registrationsettings), [SignInSettings](#signinsettings), [NotificationBellOptions](#notificationbelloptions). Authorization: [NotificationPageRequirement](#notificationpagerequirement) / [NotificationPageAuthorizationHandler](#notificationpageauthorizationhandler), [TwoFactorPageRequirement](#twofactorpagerequirement) / [TwoFactorPageAuthorizationHandler](#twofactorpageauthorizationhandler), [PagePermissionPolicyConfigurator](#pagepermissionpolicyconfigurator) / [PagePermissionAuthorizationHandler](#pagepermissionauthorizationhandler). Localization: [PseudoStringLocalizerFactory](#pseudostringlocalizerfactory), [ResxMudLocalizer](#resxmudlocalizer), [InvariantMudLocalizationInterceptor](#invariantmudlocalizationinterceptor). HTTP: [AuthDelegatingHandler](#authdelegatinghandler), [CultureDelegatingHandler](#culturedelegatinghandler), [SameOriginProxyRequestHandler](#sameoriginproxyrequesthandler), [HttpResilienceDefaults](group-16-aspire-orchestration.md#httpresiliencedefaults). Facades: [IToastService](#itoastservice) / [MudToastService](#mudtoastservice), [IAppDialogService](#iappdialogservice) / [MudAppDialogService](#mudappdialogservice), [IPendingToastService](#ipendingtoastservice) / [PendingToastService](#pendingtoastservice). Services: [IAuthUIService](#iauthuiservice) / [AuthUIService](#authuiservice) (which also backs [ISignInLinkUIService](#isigninlinkuiservice) and [IPasskeyUIService](#ipasskeyuiservice)), [IEmailConfirmationUIService](#iemailconfirmationuiservice) / [EmailConfirmationUIService](#emailconfirmationuiservice), [IOidcDiscoveryUIService](#ioidcdiscoveryuiservice) / [OidcDiscoveryUIService](#oidcdiscoveryuiservice), [ILegalAcceptanceUIService](#ilegalacceptanceuiservice) / [LegalAcceptanceUIService](#legalacceptanceuiservice), [OAuthFlowStateStore](#oauthflowstatestore), [ListPageStateService](#listpagestateservice), [ListPageQueryStateService](#listpagequerystateservice), [NavigationHistoryService](#navigationhistoryservice), [ThemeService](#themeservice), [ICultureApplier](#icultureapplier) / [EndpointCultureApplier](#endpointcultureapplier), [ViewerTimeZone](#viewertimezone), [IPublicLinkBuilder](#ipubliclinkbuilder) / [NavigationPublicLinkBuilder](#navigationpubliclinkbuilder), [IUserPreferenceWriter](#iuserpreferencewriter) / [ApiUserPreferenceWriter](#apiuserpreferencewriter), [IUserPreferenceReader](#iuserpreferencereader) / [ApiUserPreferenceReader](#apiuserpreferencereader), [IOAuthUISettings](#ioauthuisettings) / [DefaultOAuthUISettings](#defaultoauthuisettings), [IForbiddenReExecutionDetector](#iforbiddenreexecutiondetector) / [NoForbiddenReExecutionDetector](#noforbiddenreexecutiondetector), [ISessionCookieSync](#isessioncookiesync) / [JsFetchSessionCookieSync](#jsfetchsessioncookiesync). Opt-ins: [IUserAdminUIService<TUserDto>](#iuseradminuiservicetuserdto) / [UserAdminService<TUserDto>](#useradminservicetuserdto), [IUserAdminActionsUIService](#iuseradminactionsuiservice), [IRoleAdminUIService](#iroleadminuiservice) / [RoleAdminService](#roleadminservice), [IMachineClientAdminUIService](#imachineclientadminuiservice) / [MachineClientAdminService](#machineclientadminservice), [IViewAsGrantsUIService](#iviewasgrantsuiservice) / [ViewAsGrantsService](#viewasgrantsservice), [IAuditHistoryUIService](#iaudithistoryuiservice) / [AuditHistoryService](#audithistoryservice), [IOfflineWriteQueue](#iofflinewritequeue) / [OfflineWriteQueue](#offlinewritequeue) / [OfflineWriteQueueOptions](#offlinewritequeueoptions) / [IOfflineWriteHandler](#iofflinewritehandler), [IFeatureFlagAdminUIService](#ifeatureflagadminuiservice) / [FeatureFlagAdminService](#featureflagadminservice) / [FeatureFlagAdminUIOptions](#featureflagadminuioptions). Capabilities: [IFormFactor](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#iformfactor) / [WasmFormFactor](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#wasmformfactor). Composition: [IUIModule](#iuimodule), [IEntityService<TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>](#ientityservicetentitydto-tidentifiertype). Externals: Scrutor (`Decorate`, `Scan`), MudBlazor, and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization` plus `Microsoft.Extensions.{Configuration, DependencyInjection, Localization, Options}` (`DependencyInjection.cs:1-27`).
- **Concept introduced, the composition root written as an `extension(T)` block.** The whole registration surface lives inside `extension(IServiceCollection services)` (`DependencyInjection.cs:37`) rather than as classic `this`-parameter extension methods; the class doc comment calls them C# extension members (`DependencyInjection.cs:31-34`). See [primer, C# extension(T) types](00-primer.md#c-extensiont-types--read-this-once) for the language mechanics, taught once. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]` assesses one consistent idiom across layers, and this file matches the other `DependencyInjection` classes in every layer of the workspace. `[Rubric §33, Developer Experience]` assesses fail-fast startup and a small number of calls per host. `[Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]` assesses whether concerns are wired once, centrally: localization, culture forwarding, authentication, page authorization and the HTTP time limit are all configured here rather than per page.
- **Walkthrough**: thirteen methods in the extension block.
  - **`AddUIShared(IConfiguration configuration)`** (`:43-257`), in order:
    - **Options.** [ApiSettings](#apisettings) binds with `.ValidateOnStart()` (`:48-50`) and `TryAddEnumerable` registers the source-generated [ApiSettingsValidator](#apisettingsvalidator) as its `IValidateOptions<ApiSettings>` (`:51`); the comment (`:45-47`) records why: the validator checks the data annotations with no reflection and no `Options.DataAnnotations` package on a WebAssembly client. A missing `ApiEndpoint` therefore fails the host at startup rather than at the first HTTP call. [LayoutSettings](#layoutsettings) binds without validation because empty defaults are acceptable (`:54-55`), and so do [LegalSettings](#legalsettings) (`:59-60`, the footer, registration-checkbox and terms-dialog links; an absent section leaves every URL empty, which renders none of them, per `:57-58`), [RegistrationSettings](#registrationsettings) (`:64-65`, the optional blocks of the shared register page; an absent section keeps every block), [SignInSettings](#signinsettings) (`:69-70`, the optional actions of the shared sign-in pages such as sign-in links under [ADR-116](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/116-identity-completions-opt-in.html); an absent section offers nothing new, per `:67-68`) and [NotificationBellOptions](#notificationbelloptions) (`:73-74`, an absent section leaving the compiled-in defaults, per `:72`).
    - **Clock.** `TryAddSingleton(TimeProvider.System)` (`:79`), the clock the notification bell and the stale-toast sweep measure against, with a comment explaining both directions of the `TryAdd` (`:76-78`): a host that already registered one, as `AddInfrastructure` does, keeps it, and a test substitutes a `FakeTimeProvider`.
    - **Page policies.** One `AddAuthorizationCore` call (`:85-101`) registers three policies: `NotificationPageRequirement.PolicyName` carrying a plain [NotificationPageRequirement](#notificationpagerequirement) (`:87-89`), `NotificationPageRequirement.ManagePolicyName` carrying one built with `NotificationPermissions.Manage` (`:90-92`), the policy for the history and compose pages, and `TwoFactorPageRequirement.PolicyName` carrying a [TwoFactorPageRequirement](#twofactorpagerequirement) (`:98-100`). `TryAddEnumerable` adds the transient [NotificationPageAuthorizationHandler](#notificationpageauthorizationhandler) and [TwoFactorPageAuthorizationHandler](#twofactorpageauthorizationhandler) (`:102-105`). The comments state the shared rule: `[Authorize]` semantics (plus `notifications:manage` for the history and compose pages), except that a host without the notification UI (no `AddNotificationUI`) lets the request reach the router, which answers 404 instead of the sign-in challenge or Access Denied (`:81-84`); the two-factor account page follows the same rule for a host without `AddTwoFactorUI`, and its policy is registered unconditionally so the page's attribute resolves in every host (`:94-97`). Then the page permission guards: `TryAddEnumerable` registers [PagePermissionPolicyConfigurator](#pagepermissionpolicyconfigurator) as a transient `IConfigureOptions<AuthorizationOptions>` (`:110-111`) and [PagePermissionAuthorizationHandler](#pagepermissionauthorizationhandler) as a transient `IAuthorizationHandler` (`:112-113`). The comment (`:107-109`, [ADR-020](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/020-permission-based-authorization.html)) explains that there is one policy per permission a page declares through [HasPagePermissionAttribute](#haspagepermissionattribute), discovered from the registered UI modules when the options are first built, so a host adds a guarded page without a registration call of its own `[Rubric §26, Front-End Security]`.
    - **Localization** ([ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html)). `AddLocalization()` (`:116`) for `IStringLocalizer<T>`, then `Decorate<IStringLocalizerFactory, PseudoStringLocalizerFactory>()` (`:123`), registered unconditionally because the pseudo-locale transform is inert under every other culture and the pseudo locale is only ever activatable in Development (`:118-122`). `TryAddTransient<MudBlazor.MudLocalizer, ResxMudLocalizer>()` (`:129`) localizes MudBlazor's own component text; the comment (`:125-128`) records why `TryAdd` is authoritative regardless of host registration order, namely that `AddMudServices` registers no `MudLocalizer` of its own and a DI resolution test guards that assumption. `AddLocalizationInterceptor<InvariantMudLocalizationInterceptor>()` (`:138`) follows immediately: MudBlazor's own default interceptor reads its built-in English strings by assigning `CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture` (invariant, then the previous value back), which writes an `AsyncLocal` culture into the calling context; on a MAUI hybrid head, where that is the main thread, nothing resets it and the app pins to its launch language even after a culture switch reloads the thread defaults. [InvariantMudLocalizationInterceptor](#invariantmudlocalizationinterceptor) reads the same resource under an explicit invariant culture instead, and registers with replace semantics so it wins whether `AddMudServices` ran before or after this call ([ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html) Decision 10) (`:131-137`).
    - **The one HTTP client.** Both delegating handlers register transient (`:142-143`). Before the client itself, `usesSameOriginProxy` is computed from the raw configuration (`:148-149`): it is true only when `Api:SameOriginApiEndpoint` carries a value, which per the comment (`:145-147`) happens only on a WebAssembly client whose Server host opted into the same-origin API proxy ([ADR-131](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/131-same-origin-api-proxy.html)) and handed that value down through `/client-config`; every other host (Server, MAUI, a WASM client of a host that did not opt in) keeps the pipeline unchanged. Then the named `"APIClient"` (`:152-175`), whose builder is kept in `apiClient` (`:152`) so a handler can be appended afterwards. Its factory resolves `IOptions<ApiSettings>` (`:159`) and sets `client.BaseAddress = new Uri(apiSettings.SameOriginApiEndpoint ?? apiSettings.ApiEndpoint!, UriKind.Absolute)` (`:164`): the same-origin proxy base, when present, replaces the gateway URL for data calls, and the comment (`:161-163`) notes the bootstrap has already resolved it to an absolute address. There is deliberately **no** hand-written endpoint guard, and the comment says why (`:154-158`): resolving `.Value` runs the `ApiSettingsValidator` registered above, so a missing `[Required]` endpoint already fails as an `OptionsValidationException`, and a second check would only give the same failure a different, less informative exception. `client.Timeout` is pinned to [HttpResilienceDefaults](group-16-aspire-orchestration.md#httpresiliencedefaults)`.TotalRequestTimeout` (`:170`), and the comment (`:166-169`) says why it matters: this is the one time limit on the client in every render mode, because WebAssembly and MAUI add no resilience handler and the Blazor web host (`AddMmcaBlazorWebHost`) removes the one `AddServiceDefaults()` puts on every factory client; it is the shared 90-second total-request timeout rather than the BCL's 100-second default `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]`. Default headers are cleared and `Accept: application/json` added (`:171-172`), and the two handlers chain in order (`:174-175`) so every outgoing call carries both the bearer token and the active UI culture as `Accept-Language` (`:140-141`). When `usesSameOriginProxy` is true, [SameOriginProxyRequestHandler](#sameoriginproxyrequesthandler) is registered transient and appended as the **innermost** handler (`:177-183`); the comment (`:179-180`) gives the reason for that position: it must see, and strip, every `Authorization` header the outer handlers or a service's `DefaultRequestHeaders` attached, and it stamps the proxy's CSRF header `[Rubric §26, Front-End Security]`.
    - **Facades.** `services.AddCommonUiFacades()` (`:187`), factored out so a bUnit harness can register exactly these three without pulling in the whole shared-UI surface (`:185-186`).
    - **Scoped services**, all via `TryAdd` so several composing hosts cannot double-register: [IAuthUIService](#iauthuiservice) to [AuthUIService](#authuiservice) (`:190`); [IEmailConfirmationUIService](#iemailconfirmationuiservice) to [EmailConfirmationUIService](#emailconfirmationuiservice) (`:194`, the `/confirm-email` page's client per [ADR-116](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/116-identity-completions-opt-in.html); a separate interface rather than new `IAuthUIService` members, so a consumer's own `IAuthUIService` implementation keeps compiling, per the comment at `:192-193`); [ISignInLinkUIService](#isigninlinkuiservice) (`:198`) and [IPasskeyUIService](#ipasskeyuiservice) (`:203`, [ADR-139](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/139-passkeys-webauthn-opt-in-sign-in.html)), both mapped onto the framework's `AuthUIService` so a redeemed link or a passkey sign-in stores its tokens through the same path a password sign-in does (`:196-197`, `:200-202`; the passkey client is inert until a host offers passkeys through `SignIn:OfferPasskeys` or renders the passkeys panel); [IOidcDiscoveryUIService](#ioidcdiscoveryuiservice) to [OidcDiscoveryUIService](#oidcdiscoveryuiservice) (`:207`, home-realm discovery for the sign-in page's "Sign in with your organization" step, inert until the host configures an OIDC provider that declares email domains, per `:205-206`); [ILegalAcceptanceUIService](#ilegalacceptanceuiservice) to [LegalAcceptanceUIService](#legalacceptanceuiservice) (`:211`, the terms-acceptance client behind `TermsAcceptanceGate`, registered for every host and inert until a host renders the gate, per `:209-210`); [OAuthFlowStateStore](#oauthflowstatestore) (`:215`, binding an OAuth completion to the flow this client started so a deep-linked completion code from someone else's provider round trip is dropped instead of exchanged, per `:213-214`); [ListPageStateService](#listpagestateservice) (`:216`), [ListPageQueryStateService](#listpagequerystateservice) (`:217`), [NavigationHistoryService](#navigationhistoryservice) (`:218`); [ThemeService](#themeservice) (`:221`, [ADR-028](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/028-dark-theme-mode.html)); [ICultureApplier](#icultureapplier) defaulting to [EndpointCultureApplier](#endpointcultureapplier) (`:227`); [ViewerTimeZone](#viewertimezone) (`:231`, the viewer's browser time zone, so UTC instants such as notification and session times render on the clock the person reads, per `:229-230`); [IPublicLinkBuilder](#ipubliclinkbuilder) defaulting to [NavigationPublicLinkBuilder](#navigationpubliclinkbuilder) (`:237`); and the per-user preference writer and reader, [ApiUserPreferenceWriter](#apiuserpreferencewriter) and [ApiUserPreferenceReader](#apiuserpreferencereader) (`:240-241`), documented as best-effort and a no-op for an anonymous user (`:239`). Two singletons close the list: `TryAddSingleton<IOAuthUISettings, DefaultOAuthUISettings>()` (`:245`), a no-op default that a downstream app replaces, and `TryAddSingleton<IForbiddenReExecutionDetector, NoForbiddenReExecutionDetector>()` (`:250`), the not-found page's "is this a 403 re-execution" question, which always answers false because a WebAssembly or MAUI head has no request to read; the Blazor Web host replaces it with the request-reading one (`:247-249`).
    - **Capabilities.** `AddDeviceCapabilityDefaults()` (`:254`, [ADR-042](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/042-device-capability-abstraction.html)) so every capability contract resolves on every head, registered here specifically so MAUI and browser hosts can override afterwards under last-registration-wins (`:252-253`).
  - **`AddCommonUiFacades()`** (`:278-284`): three `TryAddScoped` calls, [IToastService](#itoastservice) to [MudToastService](#mudtoastservice) (`:280`), [IAppDialogService](#iappdialogservice) to [MudAppDialogService](#mudappdialogservice) (`:281`) and [IPendingToastService](#ipendingtoastservice) to [PendingToastService](#pendingtoastservice) (`:282`), the toast that survives a `forceLoad` navigation and is injected by the shared layout's `PendingToastHost`. Its doc comment (`:259-277`) is the clearest statement of the facade rule anywhere in the codebase: apart from the two Mud-backed implementations (and the `ConfirmationDialog` they open), the only framework types that name MudBlazor's `ISnackbar` / `IDialogService` are the `DeleteConfirmation` component, which injects `IDialogService` directly to show its typed dialog, and [StaleToastSweeper](#staletoastsweeper), which injects `ISnackbar` to remove toasts a navigation left behind (pages, other components and the `Result` helpers depend on the contracts); they are scoped to match the MudBlazor services they wrap, and the method is called both by `AddUIShared` and by the shipped bUnit base so a component test resolves the facades without the rest of the shared-UI surface.
  - **`AddClientAuthSessionCookieSync()`** (`:291-295`): one `TryAddScoped<ISessionCookieSync, JsFetchSessionCookieSync>()` (`:293`), the bridge that mirrors the client's in-memory tokens into the HttpOnly cookie read during server-side SSR prerender. Called from both the Blazor Server host and the WebAssembly client (`:286-290`).
  - **`AddWasmFormFactor()`** (`:303-304`): registers [IFormFactor](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#iformfactor) to [WasmFormFactor](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#wasmformfactor) as a singleton. The doc comment names the two alternatives (`:297-302`): `AddCommonWebFormFactor()` from `MMCA.Common.UI.Web` on the Blazor Server head, `AddMauiFormFactor()` from `MMCA.Common.UI.Maui` on the MAUI head.
  - **`AddUserAdministrationUI<TUserDto>()`** (`:321-331`), the [ADR-116](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/116-identity-completions-opt-in.html) UI opt-in for user administration: registers [IUserAdminUIService<TUserDto>](#iuseradminuiservicetuserdto) to [UserAdminService<TUserDto>](#useradminservicetuserdto) (`:323`), then forwards [IUserAdminActionsUIService](#iuseradminactionsuiservice) to the same instance rather than registering it a second time (`:327-328`), so the actions the component performs and the reads the app makes go through one instance (and one substitute, in a test), per the comment at `:325-326`. The doc comment (`:306-320`) states the call convention (once per app, after `AddUIShared`, with the app's own administration DTO) and that an app which serves no administration endpoints registers nothing and the component the service backs is simply never rendered.
  - **`AddRoleAdministrationUI()`** (`:347-352`): the non-generic [ADR-116](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/116-identity-completions-opt-in.html) sibling, registering [IRoleAdminUIService](#iroleadminuiservice) to [RoleAdminService](#roleadminservice) (`:349`). Its doc comment (`:333-346`) explains why it takes no type parameter unlike `AddUserAdministrationUI<TUserDto>()`: roles and permissions are strings the framework already owns, so there is no app DTO to name (`:340-341`).
  - **`AddMachineClientAdministrationUI()`** (`:362-367`), the [ADR-140](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/140-machine-clients-oauth-client-credentials.html) opt-in: [IMachineClientAdminUIService](#imachineclientadminuiservice) to [MachineClientAdminService](#machineclientadminservice) (`:364`), the client the `MachineClientAdmin` page reads and writes the app's `Admin/MachineClients` endpoints through (`:354-361`).
  - **`AddSupportAccessLogUI()`** (`:380-385`), the [ADR-137](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/137-read-only-view-as-support-access.html) opt-in: [IViewAsGrantsUIService](#iviewasgrantsuiservice) to [ViewAsGrantsService](#viewasgrantsservice) (`:382`), the client the `SupportAccessLog` page reads the app's `Admin/ViewAsGrants` endpoint through (`:369-379`).
  - **`AddAuditHistoryUI()`** (`:399-404`), the [ADR-075](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/075-audit-trail.html) opt-in: [IAuditHistoryUIService](#iaudithistoryuiservice) to [AuditHistoryService](#audithistoryservice) (`:401`), the HTTP client an `AuditHistoryPanel`'s `FetchPage` delegate reads an `AuditHistoryControllerBase` endpoint through; the doc comment (`:387-398`) adds that calling it again changes nothing and an app's own registration made first is kept.
  - **`AddOfflineWriteQueue(Action<OfflineWriteQueueOptions>? configure = null)`** (`:417-429`): the opt-in durable offline write queue ([ADR-144](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/144-offline-writes-and-delta-reads.html)). It registers [IOfflineWriteQueue](#iofflinewritequeue) to [OfflineWriteQueue](#offlinewritequeue) scoped (`:419`), because the browser connectivity service and local store it reads are scoped (`:407-408`), `TimeProvider.System` unless one is registered (`:420`), and [OfflineWriteQueueOptions](#offlinewritequeueoptions) with the optional callback applied (`:422-426`). The doc comment (`:406-414`) notes that Common's `MainLayout` already hosts the `OfflineWriteNotifier` that drains and reports the queue.
  - **`AddOfflineWriteHandler<THandler>()`** (`:437-443`), constrained to `THandler : class, IOfflineWriteHandler` (`:438`): one `TryAddEnumerable` of a scoped [IOfflineWriteHandler](#iofflinewritehandler) (`:440`), the replay handler for one write kind, so registering the same handler type again adds nothing (`:431-434`).
  - **`AddFeatureFlagAdministrationUI(params string[] sources)`** (`:458-467`), the [ADR-031](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/031-feature-flag-management.html) opt-in: guards `sources` (`:460`), registers [IFeatureFlagAdminUIService](#ifeatureflagadminuiservice) to [FeatureFlagAdminService](#featureflagadminservice) (`:462`) and appends the sources to [FeatureFlagAdminUIOptions](#featureflagadminuioptions)`.Sources` (`:463-464`). Each source is the API route prefix of one service's `FeatureFlagsControllerBase` (for example `Admin/Conference/FeatureFlags`), so a multi-service host lists every service's flags in one table (`:451-453`).
  - **`AddUIModule<TModule>()`** (`:487-497`), constrained to `TModule : class, IUIModule` (`:488`): a Scrutor scan `FromAssemblyOf<TModule>()` registering every [IEntityService<TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>](#ientityservicetentitydto-tidentifiertype) implementation scoped as its implemented interfaces (`:490-494`), then `AddSingleton<IUIModule, TModule>()` (`:496`). The doc comment (`:469-482`) records the deliberate boundary: this is the two-step prologue every module's `Add{Module}UI()` opens with, and module-specific services stay with the caller **afterwards**, so a module whose service must beat a shared default still controls its own registration order. The type-parameter doc (`:483-486`) states the constraint that follows from using the descriptor's assembly as the scan root: it must live alongside the module's entity services and Razor pages. That same `IUIModule` registration is what [PagePermissionPolicyConfigurator](#pagepermissionpolicyconfigurator) enumerates to find guarded pages.
- **Why it's built this way**: `TryAdd` throughout is both a safety property (several composing hosts calling `AddUIShared` cannot double-register) and the override mechanism (a host that registers its own implementation **before** the call wins). Several ordering choices push in the opposite direction and are called out in comments because they are load-bearing: [ICultureApplier](#icultureapplier)'s default round-trips a server `/culture/set` endpoint that a MAUI hybrid head does not have, so hybrids override it **after** `AddUIShared` (`:223-226`); [IPublicLinkBuilder](#ipubliclinkbuilder)'s default resolves against the browser origin, which is wrong for a MAUI WebView whose origin is a virtual host nobody else can open, so that is overridden after as well (`:233-236`); and [IForbiddenReExecutionDetector](#iforbiddenreexecutiondetector)'s default answers false everywhere until the Blazor Web host replaces it (`:247-249`). [InvariantMudLocalizationInterceptor](#invariantmudlocalizationinterceptor) follows the same head-dependent pattern one layer down: MudBlazor's own interceptor is correct everywhere except the MAUI hybrid main thread, so the replacement is registered unconditionally here rather than left to the affected head to override, because replace semantics make the registration order irrelevant (`:131-138`). [SameOriginProxyRequestHandler](#sameoriginproxyrequesthandler) is the one registration decided by configuration rather than by order: it is added only when `Api:SameOriginApiEndpoint` is present (`:148-149`, `:177-183`), so a host that never opts in carries no trace of it in its pipeline. The page permission policies avoid ordering altogether by deferring discovery to options build time (`:107-111`). Read together, the file encodes a rule worth carrying into any new registration: a contract whose correct implementation depends on the *head* is defaulted here and replaced later (or, where replace semantics make order irrelevant, registered outright), while a contract that is the same everywhere is `TryAdd`ed and left alone. The opt-ins follow the same principle one level up: nothing else in the framework calls any of them (`:315-316`, `:342-343`, `:358-359`, `:375-376`, `:394-395`, `:413`, `:453`), so an app that serves none of those endpoints registers nothing and the corresponding component is simply never rendered.
- **Where it's used**: called once at startup by all six consuming UI hosts (ADC's `MMCA.ADC.UI.Web`, `MMCA.ADC.UI.Web.Client` and MAUI `MMCA.ADC.UI`, plus the three Store equivalents), each followed by the per-module `Add{Module}UI()` calls, which are usually one-liners over `AddUIModule<TModule>()`, for example `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:24` and `MMCA.Store/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.Store.Identity.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:19`. `AddCommonUiFacades()` has a second caller outside any host, the shipped bUnit base (`MMCA.Common/Source/Hosting/MMCA.Common.Testing.UI/Infrastructure/BunitComponentTestBase.cs:54`). The administration, audit, offline and feature-flag opt-ins are each meant to be called once per app, after `AddUIShared` (for example `:311`, `:338`), by an app that opts into the corresponding surface; nothing inside the framework itself calls any of them. The `"APIClient"` configured here is the client every [EntityServiceBase<TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>](#entityservicebasetentitydto-tidentifiertype)-derived service resolves. The assembly this class lives in is also the one [UISharedAssemblyReference](#uisharedassemblyreference) names for the architecture fitness suite.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the Store citation (`MMCA.Store/.../MMCA.Store.Identity.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:19`) is carried over from the prior section and was not re-read in this pass; MMCA.Store is outside this guide's verified scope.

### BreakpointConstants

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Common` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/BreakpointConstants.cs:9` · Level 0 · class (static)

- **What it is**: a one-method static helper that answers "is this viewport a mobile viewport?", so C# viewport detection and the CSS media-query boundary agree on one number.
- **Depends on**: `MudBlazor.Breakpoint` (NuGet, imported at `BreakpointConstants.cs:1`). Nothing first-party.
- **Concept introduced, the single authoritative breakpoint.** `[Rubric §22, Responsive & Cross-Browser]` assesses whether a codebase has one definition of "small screen" rather than a magic number re-chosen per component; this class embodies it by making the mobile/desktop split a named predicate. The doc comment (`BreakpointConstants.cs:11-15`) pins the threshold as MudBlazor's Xs or Sm breakpoint (< 960 px) and states plainly that this is **not** the sidebar boundary: the layout's sidebar collapses separately, below 1024 px. So this class is the one definition of "mobile" for the data-grid-versus-cards switch, not for every responsive decision. `[Rubric §20, Design System & Theming]` applies for the same reason: one named threshold keeps every list page switching modes at the same width instead of at slightly different ones.
- **Walkthrough**: the type has exactly one member. `IsMobileBreakpoint(Breakpoint breakpoint)` (`BreakpointConstants.cs:16-17`) is expression-bodied and returns `breakpoint is Breakpoint.Xs or Breakpoint.Sm`. That pattern is the whole rule: `Md` and wider is desktop, and there is no third state.
- **Why it's built this way**: static and dependency-free, so a component can call it without injecting anything, and moving the mobile threshold is a one-line edit rather than a hunt through component code.
- **Where it's used**: exactly one production call site, [DataGridListPageBase<TDto>](#datagridlistpagebasetdto)'s viewport-change handler `NotifyBrowserViewportChangeAsync` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Common/DataGridListPageBase.cs:410`), which sets `IsMobile` from it at line 414 and, on a desktop-to-mobile transition, resets `MobileCurrentPage` to 1 and re-requests the mobile data (`DataGridListPageBase.cs:416-420`). That single assignment is what swaps a desktop `MudDataGrid` for the [MobileInfiniteScrollList<TItem>](#mobileinfinitescrolllisttitem) card layout on every list page in both consumer apps.

### ComponentLifetimeExtensions

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Common` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/ComponentLifetimeExtensions.cs:18` · Level 0 · class (static, extension methods)

- **What it is**: one extension method, `LifetimeToken(this CancellationTokenSource?)`, that gives a component a cancellation token it can read at any point of its lifetime without risking an exception.
- **Depends on**: `System.Threading.CancellationTokenSource`, `CancellationToken` and `ObjectDisposedException` (BCL). Nothing first-party.
- **Concept introduced, the always-safe lifetime token.** `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]` assesses whether a recurring hazard has one shared answer. Reading `CancellationTokenSource.Token` after `Dispose()` throws `ObjectDisposedException`, and a Blazor component's async continuation can easily run after the component is gone. The extension converts that failure mode into the correct behavior: a component that has ended gets a token that is already cancelled, so the in-flight call stops instead of throwing out of a dead render tree.
- **Walkthrough**: `LifetimeToken` (`ComponentLifetimeExtensions.cs:26-42`) has three outcomes. A `null` source, or one whose `IsCancellationRequested` is already true, returns `new CancellationToken(canceled: true)` (`:28-31`). Otherwise it returns `source.Token` (`:35`) inside a `try`; an `ObjectDisposedException` (a source disposed without being cancelled first) is caught and also returns a cancelled token (`:37-41`), with the comment that the component is gone all the same.
- **Why it's built this way**: an extension on the nullable source, rather than a wrapper type, so a component keeps its familiar `_cts` field and writes `_cts.LifetimeToken()` where it used to write `_cts.Token`. `null` is treated as ended (`:28`), which covers a component whose source was never created.
- **Where it's used**: [LatestLoadGuard](#latestloadguard) reads its token through it (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/LatestLoadGuard.cs:58`), and the `ResultUiExtensions` examples show `_cts.LifetimeToken()` as the call-site shape (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/ResultUiExtensions.cs:47`, `:63`). The convention is enforced by `ArchitectureRules.ComponentsReadTheirTokenThroughLifetimeToken` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Hosting/MMCA.Common.Testing.Architecture/Rules/Ui/ArchitectureRules.LifetimeTokens.cs:28`), which fails the build on a direct `_cts.Token` read, wrapped for subclassing by `LifetimeTokenConventionTestsBase` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Hosting/MMCA.Common.Testing.Architecture/Bases/Ui/LifetimeTokenConventionTestsBase.cs:13`). It is on the shipped public surface (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/PublicAPI.Shipped.txt:1391`).

### LatestLoadGuard

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Common` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/LatestLoadGuard.cs:38` · Level 0 · class (sealed, `IDisposable`)

- **What it is**: a small per-page helper that keeps a routed component showing the load it asked for **last**, by giving every load a generation number and a cancellation token and cancelling the previous one as the next begins.
- **Depends on**: `System.Threading.CancellationTokenSource` and `ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf` (BCL), and [ComponentLifetimeExtensions](#componentlifetimeextensions) for the token it hands out.
- **Concept introduced, generation-guarded supersession.** `[Rubric §19, State Management & Data Flow]` assesses the correctness of in-flight asynchronous state, and this is the canonical bug it looks for. The doc comment states it precisely (`LatestLoadGuard.cs:5-10`): Blazor **reuses a routed component instance** across route-parameter changes, so a page that opens entity 100 (slow response) and then navigates to entity 101 (fast response) receives 100's late answer after 101 has already rendered. Assigning it unconditionally leaves the URL on 101 while the page holds 100, and any action bound to the loaded entity then fires against the wrong record. Cancellation alone does not fix this, because a fetch that ignores its token still completes; the integer generation is the authoritative check. The same pattern appears at component scope inside [MobileInfiniteScrollList<TItem>](#mobileinfinitescrolllisttitem), which snapshots a generation before awaiting and drops the result if the world moved; `LatestLoadGuard` is that idea extracted into a reusable object so a detail page gets it in three lines. `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]` applies: the alternative is every page hand-rolling a token source, a counter and a dispose path.
- **Walkthrough**: three private fields (`LatestLoadGuard.cs:40-42`): the current `CancellationTokenSource?`, the `int _generation`, and a `_disposed` flag.
  - `Begin()` (`:50-59`) is the entry point. It throws if the guard is disposed (`:52`), cancels and disposes the previous load through the private `CancelAndDisposeCurrent()` (`:54`), publishes a fresh token source (`:55`), increments the generation (`:56`), and returns the pair `(CancellationToken Token, int Generation)` (`:58`), with the token read as `_cts.LifetimeToken()` rather than `_cts.Token` (`:58`) so it is the always-safe token of [ComponentLifetimeExtensions](#componentlifetimeextensions). Returning a tuple rather than exposing two properties is what makes the generation a **snapshot**: the caller holds the value it started with, so a later `Begin()` cannot retroactively change what it compares against.
  - `IsCurrent(int generation)` (`:67`) is the check after the await: `!_disposed && generation == _generation`. Disposal counts as not-current, so a component torn down mid-fetch also drops its answer instead of assigning into a dead render tree.
  - `Dispose()` (`:70-79`) is idempotent via the `_disposed` early return (`:72-75`) and cancels the in-flight load on the way out.
  - `CancelAndDisposeCurrent()` (`:81-91`) null-guards, then cancels, disposes and nulls the source, so the guard never double-disposes a token source and never leaks one.
  - The usage shape is spelled out as a `<code>` block in the doc comment (`:15-31`): a `private readonly LatestLoadGuard _load = new();` field, `var (token, generation) = _load.Begin();` at the top of `OnParametersSetAsync`, an `if (!_load.IsCurrent(generation)) { return; }` immediately after the await, and `public void Dispose() => _load.Dispose();`.
- **Why it's built this way**: deliberately **not thread-safe**, and the doc comment says so in bold (`:32-36`). It is built for the renderer's synchronization context, where component lifecycle methods and event callbacks are already serialized, so the fields need no interlocking and the type stays allocation-cheap. That is a contract, not an oversight: sharing one instance across threads is documented as unsupported.
- **Where it's used**: the framework's `DetailPageBase` exposes one as `protected LatestLoadGuard LoadGuard { get; } = new();` and disposes it (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Common/DetailPageBase.cs:34`, `:95`), so every detail page derived from it inherits the guard. `RoleAdminEdit` holds its own `_load` and runs the `Begin()` / `IsCurrent(generation)` shape directly (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Administration/RoleAdminEdit.razor.cs:42`, `:162`, `:174`, `:187`), and ADC's public event, session and speaker detail pages and `SessionCreate` also call it (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Public/Events/PublicEventDetail.razor.cs`, `Pages/Public/Sessions/PublicSessionDetail.razor.cs`, `Pages/Public/Speakers/PublicSpeakerDetail.razor.cs`, `Pages/Sessions/SessionCreate.razor.cs`). It is on the shipped public surface (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/PublicAPI.Shipped.txt:37-41`). It is also exercised by [LatestLoadGuardTests](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Common/LatestLoadGuardTests.cs:11`, six test methods covering `Begin` cancelling the prior token, generation advance, `IsCurrent` after supersession, and behavior after disposal) `[Rubric §28, Front-End Testing]`; `DetailPageBaseTests` covers the base-class wiring (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Pages/Common/DetailPageBaseTests.cs`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the guard is not thread-safe by contract, and a page that bypasses it (assigning a fetch result unconditionally) is not caught by any analyzer; adoption is by `DetailPageBase` inheritance or by hand, as `RoleAdminEdit` does.

### NavGroup

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Common` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/NavGroup.cs:23` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the optional rendering description of one collapsible sidebar group, keyed by the [NavItem](#navitem) `Group` string: its icon, whether it starts expanded, and its position within its section.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party at compile time (its doc comment cross-references [NavItem](#navitem) and [IUIModule](#iuimodule)).
- **Concept introduced, describing a group by key rather than by ownership.** `[Rubric §25, Navigation & Information Architecture]` assesses whether a menu's structure is declared rather than hard-coded. A group has no owner: it exists because items carry the same `Group` key, and the doc comment (`NavGroup.cs:8-12`) makes the consequence explicit. A module may describe a group whose items **another** module contributes (for example a framework-owned entry an app wants to place), the first registered description of a key wins, and a group nobody describes renders as before: the folder icon, collapsed, in the order its first item appears. `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]` applies through what the record deliberately does not carry: no display text. The heading is still the `Key` resolved against the first item's `TitleResource` (`NavGroup.cs:14-17`, [ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html)).
- **Walkthrough**: a positional record on one line (`NavGroup.cs:23`) with four parameters, three optional.
  - `string Key`: the `NavItem.Group` value the description applies to.
  - `string? Icon = null`: `null` keeps the folder icon.
  - `bool Expanded = false`: whether the group starts expanded.
  - `int Order = 0`: the group's position among the units of its section, where each group and the section's ungrouped items (which count as order 0) are units; ties keep first-appearance order (`NavGroup.cs:4-6`, `:22`).
- **Why it's built this way**: a separate record rather than more parameters on [NavItem](#navitem), so group metadata is stated once per group instead of repeated on every item, and so an app can arrange a group it does not own. Every member defaults to the old behavior, so a host that declares no group renders exactly as it did. The menu realizes it in two steps: `NavMenu.OnInitializedAsync` collects every module's `NavGroups` with `TryAdd`, which is the first-registered-wins rule (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Layout/NavMenu.razor.cs:79-83`), and the private `Arrange` groups a section by key in first-appearance order, applies the description's `Icon ?? Icons.Material.Filled.Folder`, `Expanded ?? false` and `Order ?? 0` to each [NavUnit](#navunit), then stable-sorts the units by `Order` (`NavMenu.razor.cs:51-66`).
- **Where it's used**: declared through the defaulted `IReadOnlyList<NavGroup> NavGroups => []` member of [IUIModule](#iuimodule) (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/Interfaces/IUIModule.cs:22`) and consumed by [NavMenu](#navmenu). ADC's `ConferenceUIModule` is the consumer example: it describes its organizer layout, with Conference Day and Program starting expanded and the framework's Notifications group placed last (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/ConferenceUIModule.cs:95-99`). Covered by `NavMenuOrderingTests` (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Layout/NavMenuOrderingTests.cs:39`, `:82`, `:101`, `:124`), which pins the undescribed default, a described icon and expanded state, group ordering with ties, and the first-declaration-wins rule across modules `[Rubric §28, Front-End Testing]`. [ADR-067](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/067-ui-module-shell-composition.html) records the UI shell composition it belongs to.

### NavSection

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Common` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/NavSection.cs:7` · Level 0 · enum

- **What it is**: classifies a sidebar entry into one of three audience groups: everyone, signed-in users, or administrators.
- **Depends on**: nothing. Consumed by [NavItem](#navitem) and by the shared nav menu.
- **Concept introduced, audience as a first-class navigation axis.** `[Rubric §25, Navigation & Information Architecture]` assesses whether the menu structure is declarative and audience-aware rather than a hand-maintained pile of conditionals. `[Rubric §11, Security]` touches it too, but with an important distinction worth internalizing early: the section is a **grouping hint, not an authorization check**. What actually hides a link is `RequiredRole` / `RequiredClaim` on [NavItem](#navitem), evaluated by the menu (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Layout/NavMenu.razor.cs:125-126`), and what actually protects the destination is page-level and API-level authorization.
- **Walkthrough**: three values in declaration order, and the order is itself a contract because the doc comment states sections render in enum declaration order (`NavSection.cs:5`). `General` (`:10`) is for items visible to everyone, anonymous and authenticated alike. `User` (`:13`) is for signed-in non-admin items. `Admin` (`:16`) is for administrator items.
- **Why it's built this way**: an enum rather than a string gives the renderer exhaustive, typo-proof matching, which is exactly what `NavMenu.razor.cs` relies on when it partitions the flattened item list into three sections with `i.Section is NavSection.General` / `User` / `Admin`, arranging each one into its units (`NavMenu.razor.cs:130-132`). It is a plain C# enum rather than a smart enumeration because no member needs to carry data or behavior, which is the default this codebase commits to ([ADR-104](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/104-smart-enums-as-opt-in-capability.html)).
- **Where it's used**: the `Section` parameter of [NavItem](#navitem) (`NavItem.cs:16`, defaulting to `General`), and the three-way partition at `NavMenu.razor.cs:130-132`. [NotificationUIModule](#notificationuimodule) shows both non-default values in one file: its inbox item is `Section: NavSection.User` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Notifications/NotificationUIModule.cs:19`) and its push-management item is `Section: NavSection.Admin` (`:20`).

### PersistedTally

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Common` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/PrerenderStateBudget.cs:104` · Level 0 · class (private sealed, nested in [PrerenderStateBudget](#prerenderstatebudget))

- **What it is**: the per-state running total behind [PrerenderStateBudget](#prerenderstatebudget)'s page-wide cap: the set of keys already persisted into one `PersistentComponentState` and the UTF-8 JSON bytes they add up to.
- **Depends on**: `HashSet<string>` and `StringComparer.Ordinal` (BCL). Nothing first-party.
- **Concept introduced**: none of its own; the budget concept is taught at [PrerenderStateBudget](#prerenderstatebudget). What this type adds is how a pass boundary is detected without any hook from the framework.
- **Walkthrough**: two fields, `_keys` (an ordinal `HashSet<string>`, `PrerenderStateBudget.cs:106`) and `_totalBytes` (`:107`).
  - `Fits(string key, int bytes, int budget)` (`:113-122`): if `key` is already in the set, the tally clears both fields first (`:115-119`), because one persistence pass cannot persist a key twice, so a repeat marks a later pass over the same state instance (`:110-111`). It then returns `_totalBytes + bytes <= budget` (`:121`).
  - `Add(string key, int bytes)` (`:124-128`) records the key and adds its bytes.
- **Why it's built this way**: split into a check and a commit so the caller can count a key only after `PersistAsJson` has accepted it (`PrerenderStateBudget.cs:95-98`), leaving the tally untouched if the write throws. It holds no lock itself; the caller locks the instance around both calls (`:86`).
- **Where it's used**: only inside [PrerenderStateBudget](#prerenderstatebudget), which keeps one per state in a `ConditionalWeakTable<PersistentComponentState, PersistedTally>` (`PrerenderStateBudget.cs:51`) and creates it on first use (`:85`). Exercised indirectly through `PrerenderStateBudgetTests` (see [PrerenderStateBudget](#prerenderstatebudget)).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the restart-on-repeated-key rule has no dedicated test: no call in `PrerenderStateBudgetTests.cs` persists the same key twice into one state (its calls at `:33-34`, `:56-58`, `:83`, `:90` all use distinct keys per state).

### RoutePaths

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Common` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/RoutePaths.cs:7` · Level 0 · class (static)

- **What it is**: the route-path constants owned by the shared UI package itself. Module-specific routes live in their own `*RoutePaths` classes.
- **Depends on**: nothing.
- **Concept introduced, one source of truth for route strings.** `[Rubric §25, Navigation & Information Architecture]` also covers URL hygiene: a literal `"/profile/sessions"` typed into four components is four places to get a rename wrong. The class comment (`RoutePaths.cs:3-6`) states both halves of the convention: centralized paths shared across all UI modules and hosts live here, and module-specific paths live in their own class. That convention is followed consistently across the workspace, by [NotificationRoutePaths](#notificationroutepaths) in this package and by `ConferenceRoutePaths`, `EngagementRoutePaths` and `IdentityRoutePaths` in the consumer modules.
- **Walkthrough**: two `public static readonly string` members.
  - `Home = "/"` (`RoutePaths.cs:9`).
  - `Sessions = "/profile/sessions"` (`:16`), the signed-in-devices page. Its doc comment (`:11-15`) records why it belongs to the framework rather than to an app: the page is framework-owned (`MMCA.Common.UI.Pages.Auth.Sessions`), lists the user's live refresh sessions with per-device and account-wide sign-out, and is reachable from the shared nav menu's authenticated section, so a consuming app gets it without doing any routing work.
- **Why it's built this way**: `static readonly` rather than `const` is sufficient because these strings are consumed in navigation and `Href` expressions, not in attribute arguments. That has one consequence worth knowing: a `@page` directive still needs its own literal, so `Home.razor:1` writes `@page "/"` directly and this constant covers only the linking and navigating side. `Sessions` shows the cost of the convention: the route literal appears in the page's own `@page` directive and again here, and only the tests hold the two together.
- **Where it's used**: `RoutePaths.Home` backs the navbar brand link (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Layout/NavMenu.razor:18`), the Home nav link (`NavMenu.razor:58`), and the first breadcrumb of the sessions page (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Auth/Sessions.razor.cs:74`). `RoutePaths.Sessions` backs the authenticated-section nav link (`NavMenu.razor:142`) and is asserted by name in both repos' component tests: `MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Layout/NavMenuTests.cs:76` pins that the link renders inside `.nav-auth-section`, `:75` pins its position, `:88` pins that it is absent for an anonymous user, and `MMCA.Store/Tests/Modules/Identity/MMCA.Store.Identity.UI.Tests/Pages/Users/Profile/ProfileTests.cs:67` pins that the profile page links to it.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: `Sessions` is still listed in `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt:339`) while `Home` is baselined in `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt:916`, so the two members sit at different points in the public-API baseline cycle.

### NavItem

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Common` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/NavItem.cs:20` · Level 1 · record

- **What it is**: the immutable description of one sidebar entry a UI module contributes: title, href, icon, the resource type its title resolves against, optional role, claim and permission gates, its [NavSection](#navsection), an optional collapsible group, and an optional sort position.
- **Depends on**: [NavSection](#navsection); `System.Type` (BCL).
- **Concept introduced, navigation as data contributed by modules.** `[Rubric §25, Navigation & Information Architecture]` assesses modular, role-aware navigation. The shared menu never knows which modules exist: it flattens every injected module's `NavItems`, filters, partitions into sections and arranges each one (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Layout/NavMenu.razor.cs:123-132`). That mirrors the server-side [IModule](group-14-module-system-composition.md#imodule) contract one layer up ([ADR-059](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/059-module-contract-and-composition.html) for the server, [ADR-067](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/067-ui-module-shell-composition.html) for this one). `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]` applies through `TitleResource` ([ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html)). `[Rubric §11, Security]` and [ADR-020](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/020-permission-based-authorization.html) apply through `RequiredPermission`.
- **Walkthrough**: a positional record (`NavItem.cs:20`) with nine parameters, five of them optional, plus one `init` property in its body:
  - `Title`, `Href`, `Icon`: required, positional.
  - `Type TitleResource`: **required**, and the fourth positional parameter. This is the localization contract, and the doc comment states it precisely (`NavItem.cs:13-18`): `Title` and `Group` are resource **keys**, resolved against `TitleResource` at render time, per-circuit, so the menu follows the active culture. A key the resource type does not declare renders as the raw string, which is what makes a not-yet-translated entry legible instead of blank. `NavMenu` implements exactly that, calling `LocalizerFactory.Create(item.TitleResource)[item.Title]` for an item (`NavMenu.razor.cs:29-33`) and resolving a group heading against the resource of the group's first registered item (`NavMenu.razor.cs:35-46`, `:59`), with the ADR-027 rule restated in a code comment at `:26-28`.
  - `string? RequiredRole = null` and `string? RequiredClaim = null`: render gates. The menu applies them as `item.RequiredRole is null || _user?.IsInRole(item.RequiredRole) == true` and the equivalent claim-type test (`NavMenu.razor.cs:125-126`).
  - `string? RequiredPermission = null`: a third, permission-based render gate, layered on top of role and claim. The menu applies it as `item.RequiredPermission is null || _user.HasPermissionClaim(item.RequiredPermission)` (`NavMenu.razor.cs:127`), the same permission-claim mechanism [ADR-020](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/020-permission-based-authorization.html) uses on the write side, so a nav entry can be hidden by permission instead of only by role.
  - `NavSection Section = NavSection.General`: which sidebar section the item lands in (`NavMenu.razor.cs:130-132`).
  - `string? Group = null`: nests the item inside a collapsible `MudNavGroup`; the menu's private `Arrange` groups each section by it with `GroupBy(item => item.Group)` (`NavMenu.razor.cs:53`), and a [NavGroup](#navgroup) with the same key can describe that group's icon, initial state and position.
  - `int Order { get; init; }` (`NavItem.cs:22-27`): the item's position within its group, or within its section's ungrouped items. `Arrange` sorts each unit's items with a stable `OrderBy(item => item.Order)` (`NavMenu.razor.cs:63`), so ties keep registration order and an app that sets no order renders as it would without the property.
- **Why it's built this way**: a positional record gives value semantics and a one-line construction per entry, which is what makes a module's `NavItems` read as a small declarative list. Making `TitleResource` a **required positional** parameter rather than an optional nullable one is the load-bearing design choice: there is no way to register a nav item that bypasses localization, so "all visible text follows the selected language" holds for the menu by construction rather than by review. [ADR-067](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/067-ui-module-shell-composition.html) records the shape at this exact line (`NavItem.cs:20`). `RequiredPermission` is a third, independent gate rather than folded into `RequiredClaim`, so a caller can express "hide by permission" without hand-building the permission claim type/value pair itself. `Order` sits in the record body rather than among the positional parameters, so it changed no constructor signature (`NavItem.cs:22-25`) and is set with an object initializer, `new(...) { Order = 1 }`.
- **Where it's used**: returned from the `NavItems` property of every [IUIModule](#iuimodule) implementation (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/Interfaces/IUIModule.cs:14`) and rendered by [NavMenu](#navmenu). [NotificationUIModule](#notificationuimodule) is the framework's own example and shows both the minimal and the maximal form: `new("Nav.NotificationInbox", NotificationRoutePaths.NotificationInbox, Icons.Material.Filled.Inbox, typeof(SharedResource), Section: NavSection.User)` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Notifications/NotificationUIModule.cs:19`) and `new("Nav.PushNotifications", NotificationRoutePaths.Notifications, Icons.Material.Filled.NotificationsActive, typeof(SharedResource), RequiredPermission: NotificationPermissions.Manage, Section: NavSection.Admin, Group: "Nav.Group.Notifications")` (`:20`). ADC's `ConferenceUIModule` shows `Order` in use across all three sections, for example `{ Order = -50 }` on its first public entry and `{ Order = 1 }` through `{ Order = 4 }` inside each admin group (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/ConferenceUIModule.cs:56`, `:79-92`). Covered by [NavMenuTests](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Layout/NavMenuTests.cs`), which drives the menu through a `StubUiModule(IReadOnlyList<NavItem> navItems)` (`:308`), and by `NavMenuOrderingTests` (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Layout/NavMenuOrderingTests.cs:138`) for item ordering with ties.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: `RequiredRole` and `RequiredClaim` control **rendering only**. They hide a link; they do not authorize the destination. The menu keeps a section-level authentication check alongside the per-item one deliberately (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Layout/NavMenu.razor:118`), but page-level and API-level authorization remain the enforcing gates.

### PrerenderStateBudget

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Common` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/PrerenderStateBudget.cs:20` · Level 1 · class (static, extension method)

- **What it is**: one extension method on `PersistentComponentState`, `TryPersistAsJsonWithinBudget`, that persists a component's prerender state only when it fits both a per-key cap and a page-wide total, so the circuit-start message never outgrows SignalR's limit.
- **Depends on**: `PersistentComponentState` (ASP.NET Core Components), `System.Text.Json` (`JsonSerializer`, `JsonDocument`, `JsonSerializerOptions`) and `ConditionalWeakTable` (BCL); its nested [PersistedTally](#persistedtally).
- **Concept introduced, a byte budget for prerendered state.** `[Rubric §12, Performance and Scalability]` assesses whether a resource limit is designed for rather than discovered in production, and `[Rubric §19, State Management & Data Flow]` whether handed-over client state has a bound. The class doc states the failure precisely (`PrerenderStateBudget.cs:7-13`): on a Blazor Server circuit the browser sends every component's persisted state back inside the SignalR message that starts the circuit, and a message over the hub's `MaximumReceiveMessageSize` (32 KB by default) closes the connection, so the page reconnects, sends the same state again and never becomes interactive, with only a Debug-level `InvalidDataException` as a trace. The remedy rests on one safe fallback (`:15-18`): skipping is always correct, because a component that finds nothing to restore fetches on its interactive pass exactly as it would without a prerender. [ADR-056](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/056-blazor-render-mode-strategy.html) records this budget as part of the render-mode strategy.
- **Walkthrough**:
  - `MaxJsonBytes = 14 * 1024` (`PrerenderStateBudget.cs:30`): the per-key cap, under half of the 32 KB limit. The doc comment (`:22-29`) shows the arithmetic: each value is base64 inside the state dictionary, which is Data Protection protected and base64 encoded again, so a JSON byte costs about 16/9 of a byte on the wire and 14 KB of JSON lands near 25 KB.
  - `SerializerOptions` (`:34`): `JsonSerializerDefaults.Web`, the options `PersistAsJson` and `TryTakeFromJson` use, so bytes measured here restore unchanged.
  - `MaxTotalJsonBytes = 16 * 1024` (`:45`): the page-wide total across every key persisted through this class into one state, about 28 KB on the wire. Its doc comment (`:36-44`) records why the per-key cap was not enough: two components each just under it (a catalog page and a grid beside it) reached 28.5 KB of the 32 KB limit.
  - `Tallies` (`:51`): a `ConditionalWeakTable<PersistentComponentState, PersistedTally>`, keyed weakly by the state object, so a tally lives exactly as long as the scope that owns the state and needs no DI registration.
  - `TryPersistAsJsonWithinBudget<TValue>(this PersistentComponentState state, string key, TValue instance, int maxJsonBytes = MaxJsonBytes)` (`:71-75`): null-guards `state` (`:77`), serializes **once** to UTF-8 (`:79`) and returns `false` over the per-key cap (`:80-83`). It then fetches or creates the state's tally (`:85`), locks it (`:86`) and returns `false` if the bytes do not fit what is left of `MaxTotalJsonBytes` (`:88-91`). Otherwise it parses the measured bytes into a `JsonDocument` and persists its `RootElement` (`:96-97`), because `PersistentComponentState` takes no raw bytes publicly and a `JsonElement` is written token for token without serializing `TValue` again (`:93-95`). Only then does it add the key to the tally (`:98`) and return `true`.
- **Why it's built this way**: an extension method, so a page calls it where it would have called `PersistAsJson` and no service is injected. The remarks (`:58-64`) state the boundaries honestly: a larger `maxJsonBytes` does not raise the page-wide budget, and a small fixed-size value persisted with `PersistAsJson` directly sits outside the total, which the headroom between 28 KB and 32 KB absorbs. It is public so a consumer page persisting its own content-sized state uses the same budget (`:17-18`).
- **Where it's used**: [DataGridListPageBase<TDto>](#datagridlistpagebasetdto)'s persisting callback calls it with the grid's [PersistedGridState](#persistedgridstate) (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Common/DataGridListPageBase.cs:252`), with a comment that a wide grid at a large page size would otherwise outgrow the circuit-start message (`:247-249`). Covered by `PrerenderStateBudgetTests` (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Common/PrerenderStateBudgetTests.cs:17`), which pins that the second of two 10 KB keys on one state is skipped (`:24`), that three 4 KB keys under the total all persist (`:48`), and that two state instances never share a total (`:69`) `[Rubric §28, Front-End Testing]`.

### ResultUiExtensions

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Common` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/ResultUiExtensions.cs:74` · Level 4 · class (static, extension methods)

- **What it is**: the page-side half of the Result transport. It is the four things a Blazor page ever does with a failed [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), written once so no page hand-rolls them again: unwrap the value, push the message into an inline alert, raise it as a toast, or branch on **why** it failed.
- **Depends on**: [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error), [ErrorType](group-01-result-error-handling.md#errortype) and [ErrorTypeSeverity](group-01-result-error-handling.md#errortypeseverity) from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions` (`ResultUiExtensions.cs:5`); `ProblemDetailsResultReader` and the synthesized-failure codes of `HttpResultExecutor` (`:6`, `:9`); [IToastService](#itoastservice) and [ToastSeverity](#toastseverity) (`:7`); the framework's `SharedResource` resource pair (`:8`); `Microsoft.Extensions.Localization.IStringLocalizer` (`:4`); `System.Resources.ResourceManager` (`:3`); `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.NotNullWhenAttribute` and `SuppressMessageAttribute` (`:1`).
- **Concept introduced, localize-with-pass-through, and severity-ordered deduplication.** `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]` assesses whether a failure reaches the user as one clear, actionable sentence; `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]` assesses whether that sentence follows the active culture; `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]` assesses whether the same five lines get re-typed per page. Two mechanisms carry all three.
  - **Pass-through localization** (`:22-27`): every message is looked up as a resource key, and one the localizer does not declare renders **verbatim**. That is what lets a single call site handle both an API error whose text the server already localized and a client-side error whose `Message` is a resource key.
  - **Code-keyed fallback for synthesized failures** (`:27-33`): a failure the client built itself, with no server-phrased message to pass through (a bodiless HTTP status, a transport failure, a client timeout), is looked up by its error **code** instead: `Http.{status}`, then the generic `Http.Status` format, `Http.TransportFailure`, `Http.Timeout`. A code the supplied localizer does not hold resolves from the framework's own `SharedResource` pair for the current UI culture, so a consumer page passing its own `IStringLocalizer<PageType>` (which holds no `Http.*` keys) still shows the translated sentence; the English message is the last resort. The class holds a private `ResourceManager SharedResources = new(typeof(SharedResource))` (`:84`) and the format key `HttpStatusFallbackKey = "Http.Status"` (`:78`) for this.
  - **Severity-ordered deduplication** (`:36-39`): messages are made distinct with `StringComparer.Ordinal` and ordered most-severe-first via [ErrorTypeSeverity](group-01-result-error-handling.md#errortypeseverity), so a real 403 or 500 leads and an incidental validation message never buries it. The shape this guards against is common once `Result.Combine` aggregates invariants: the same sentence arriving under several codes now reads as one sentence. This is the client mirror of the server-side status selection recorded in [ADR-013](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/013-result-pattern.html), using the very same ranking type hoisted into `Shared` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Shared/Abstractions/ErrorTypeSeverity.cs:59`) so both edges classify one aggregate identically.

  The class doc even ships a before/after pair (`:42-73`) contrasting the old `try` / `catch (Exception ex)` shape with `if (result.TryGetValue(out var dto)) { ... } else { result.NotifyOnFailure(Toast, L); }`, both reading the token as `_cts.LifetimeToken()` ([ComponentLifetimeExtensions](#componentlifetimeextensions)). The `TryGetValue` in that example is the instance method on [Result<T>](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) itself, not a member of this class (the class doc's bullet list says so at `:17`).
- **Walkthrough**: eleven public members plus five private helpers, in four tiers.
  - **Unwrapping.** The plain unwrap lives on the result: `Result<T>.TryGetValue([MaybeNullWhen(false)] out T value)` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Shared/Abstractions/Result.cs:218-228`) decides the branch by `IsFailure` alone and returns `true` for any success, so when `T` is itself nullable the value stays nullable on the success branch (`Result.cs:214`). This class adds only the three-argument overload `TryGetValue<T>(this Result<T>, [NotNullWhen(true)] out T? value, out IReadOnlyList<Error> errors)` (`ResultUiExtensions.cs:103-120`), whose doc cross-references the instance method (`:87`) and which hands the errors back on the failing branch. Its success test is stricter: `result.IsSuccess && result.Value is not null` (`:110`). It documents that edge honestly (`:89-96`): a *success* carrying a null value also takes the failing branch, and a success has no errors, so `errors` comes back empty. The framework's own services never produce that shape (a 2xx with no value fails with `Http.EmptyResponse`), and the renderers here treat an empty list as nothing to say rather than an empty alert, but a caller switching on the error list should not assume it is non-empty.
  - **Composing the message.** `LocalizedErrorMessages(this Result, IStringLocalizer?)` (`:132-146`) returns an empty list for a success, so a caller can bind it without a null or success check, and otherwise orders by `ErrorTypeSeverity.Rank` descending, localizes each **error** through the private `LocalizeError` (`:143`) rather than its bare message, drops blanks, and takes ordinal-distinct values (`:141-145`). `LocalizedErrorMessage` (`:156-160`) joins that list with a space and returns `null` for a success. `LocalizeDistinct(IEnumerable<string>?, IStringLocalizer?)` (`:172-184`) gives the same treatment to a plain message list, specifically the `MudForm.Errors` shape whose entries are resource keys produced by the model's DataAnnotations; it preserves original order rather than re-ranking, since those entries carry no `ErrorType`.
  - **Rendering.** `OnFailureSetError(this Result, Action<string?> setError, IStringLocalizer?)` (`:214-221`) hands the composed message to the page's own error field, the one an inline `MudAlert` or the `PageErrorState` component renders (its doc comment names it by its current home, `MMCA.Common.UI.Components.PageState.PageErrorState`, at `:187-188`, matching the file at `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/PageState/PageErrorState.razor:1`), and **clears it on success** by passing the composed message, which is `null` for a success (`:219`), which is why a retry that succeeds does not leave a stale alert on screen. `NotifyOnFailure(this Result, IToastService, IStringLocalizer?, ToastSeverity = Error)` (`:255-271`) raises the composed message as **one** toast, never one per error, calling `toast.Show(message, severity)` only when the composed message is non-null (`:264-268`). Both return the same result instance so the call can sit inline, and both have a `Result<T>` overload that delegates to the non-generic one and returns the typed result (`:226-230`, `:276-284`), which is what keeps `(await Service.AddAsync(dto, token)).NotifyOnFailure(Toast, L)` chainable. All four rendering overloads carry the same `[SuppressMessage("ApiDesign", "RS0026...")]` (`:213`, `:225`, `:254`, `:275`): two public overloads with optional parameters is the shape RS0026 forbids, and the justification records them as grandfathered, released after the v1.152 public-API baseline while RS0026/RS0027 were off, so changing the signatures now would be a breaking change.
  - **Branching on why.** `HasErrorType(this Result, ErrorType)` (`:294-298`) is the general predicate; the doc comment (`:286-289`) notes the category survives the HTTP round trip through [ProblemDetailsResultReader](group-08-auth.md#problemdetailsresultreader), which is what makes this meaningful client-side at all. `IsNotFound()` (`:306`) and `IsUnauthorized()` (`:314`) are the two named cases, and their doc comments state the intended UI reaction: a 404 becomes a "not found" state rather than an error alert, a 401 becomes a redirect to the login route.
  - **The private helpers.** `LocalizeError(Error, IStringLocalizer?)` (`:316-339`) chooses the lookup per error. With no localizer it returns the message verbatim. For a synthesized HTTP status (`ProblemDetailsResultReader.TryGetSynthesizedStatus`) it tries the status's own `Http.{status}` code, then the `Http.Status` format with the status code as argument, then the message (`:326-331`). For the executor's own transport or timeout failure it tries the code, then the message (`:333-336`); `IsSynthesizedTransportFailure` (`:366-371`) matches only when the message is still the executor's own English sentence, so a caller that reused one of those codes with a message of its own keeps it. Anything else falls to `Localize`. `LookUpByCode` (`:343`) asks the caller's localizer first and then the framework's `SharedResources`, and `FormatByCode` (`:352`) does the same for a format string. `Localize(string message, IStringLocalizer?)` (`:373-382`) is where pass-through actually happens: a null localizer or a blank message returns the input unchanged, otherwise it indexes the localizer and returns `localized.ResourceNotFound ? message : localized.Value` (`:381`).
- **Why it's built this way**: extension methods on `Result` rather than an injectable service, because there is no state and nothing to resolve, so a page uses them without a constructor parameter and a unit test calls them directly. Every rendering helper returns the result it was given, which is what allows the fluent one-liner style the class doc advertises. The nullable `IStringLocalizer?` parameter everywhere means the helpers work from a context that has no localizer (they then render verbatim) rather than forcing one in.
- **Where it's used**: by every page and component that calls an [IEntityService<TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>](#ientityservicetentitydto-tidentifiertype) member, across the framework package and both consumer apps, plus the shared deduplicating error-summary component. Covered by [ResultUiExtensionsTests](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup) (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Common/ResultUiExtensionsTests.cs:22`) `[Rubric §28, Front-End Testing]`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the class doc opens with "the Result transport (ADR-030)" (`ResultUiExtensions.cs:14`), but ADR-030 is `030-startup-sole-migrator.md`. The Result-pattern record, including the 2026-08-27 revision that names `ResultUiExtensions` and its exact member list, is [ADR-013](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/013-result-pattern.html); the client data-access half is [ADR-094](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/094-client-entity-data-access.html). Trust the ADR index over the comment.
