### ViewerTimeZone
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Culture` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Culture/ViewerTimeZone.cs:22` · Level 1 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: a scoped service that learns the viewer's browser time zone once and converts the UTC
  instants the API serializes onto the clock the person actually reads. Until the zone is known it
  reports UTC (`ViewerTimeZone.cs:36`).
- **Depends on**: [LazyJsModule](#lazyjsmodule) (held as `_module`, built over the host's `IJSRuntime` in
  the constructor, `ViewerTimeZone.cs:30`) and the `time-zone.js` module named at
  `ViewerTimeZone.cs:24`. Implements `IAsyncDisposable`.
- **Concept introduced, rendering instants on the viewer's clock.** `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]`
  assesses whether dates are shown the way the reader expects, not the way the server stores them. A
  server-side `ToLocalTime()` would use the server's zone; this service asks the browser instead.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `Zone` (`ViewerTimeZone.cs:36`) defaults to `TimeZoneInfo.Utc`; `IsResolved` (`ViewerTimeZone.cs:42`)
    stays false while JS interop is unavailable, so a later call can retry.
  - `EnsureResolvedAsync` (`ViewerTimeZone.cs:54`) returns early when already resolved, then imports the
    module and invokes `getTimeZone` (`ViewerTimeZone.cs:64-65`). JS side:
    `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/wwwroot/time-zone.js:6` returns the
    `Intl.DateTimeFormat` zone id, or null when the browser cannot say.
  - Failure handling is split by whether a retry could help. `InvalidOperationException` (SSR
    prerender, no interop yet), `JSDisconnectedException` and `OperationCanceledException` return false
    without marking resolved (`ViewerTimeZone.cs:67-80`); a `JSException` means the browser answered
    with an error, so the zone id becomes null and resolution is final (`ViewerTimeZone.cs:81-85`).
  - Once the browser has answered (successfully or not) it sets `IsResolved`, assigns `Zone` through
    the private `ResolveZone`, and returns true (`ViewerTimeZone.cs:87-89`). It returns true even when
    the zone stays UTC, because the first resolution is what turns `Format` output from the empty
    placeholder into a time, so the caller always re-renders once. `ResolveZone`
    (`ViewerTimeZone.cs:128`) falls back to UTC for a missing or unknown id.
  - `ToViewerTime` (`ViewerTimeZone.cs:100`) reads `Utc` and `Unspecified` kinds as UTC (a deserialized
    value often arrives unspecified) and normalizes `Local` first, then calls
    `TimeZoneInfo.ConvertTimeFromUtc`. `Format` (`ViewerTimeZone.cs:118`) returns `string.Empty` while
    `IsResolved` is false (prerender, and the first interactive render before `EnsureResolvedAsync`
    ran); once resolved it formats the converted value with `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture`, default
    format `"g"`.
  - `DisposeAsync` (`ViewerTimeZone.cs:122`) forwards to the module wrapper.
- **Why it's built this way**: [ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html)
  treats locale as a per-viewer concern. Returning a boolean from `EnsureResolvedAsync` keeps the
  service free of render coupling: the page calls it from `OnAfterRenderAsync` on its first render
  and decides whether to call `StateHasChanged`. Swallowing prerender interop failures lets the same
  component render on the server and then fill in after hydration; rendering an empty placeholder
  until then, rather than a UTC fallback, means a UTC time never paints only to jump to the viewer's
  clock a moment later.
- **Where it's used**: registered with `TryAddScoped<ViewerTimeZone>()`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:231`) and injected by
  `NotificationList.razor.cs:30`, `NotificationInbox.razor.cs:37` and `Sessions.razor.cs:35` under
  `MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/` and by `Components/Auth/UserSessionsTable.razor.cs:32`, plus ADC pages such
  as `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/Points/MyPoints.razor.cs`.
  Covered by `MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Services/Culture/ViewerTimeZoneTests.cs`.

### MultiFactorRequiredSignal

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Auth.TwoFactor` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Auth/TwoFactor/MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:19` · Level 2 · class (internal static)

- **What it is**: an in-process signal that carries "the API refused this session for want of a
  second factor" from the API client's message handler to the page that should react to it
  (`MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:6-12`).
- **Depends on**: [ITokenStorageService](#itokenstorageservice) (the key) and its nested
  [Subscription](#subscription). Externals: `ConditionalWeakTable<TKey, TValue>`.
- **Concept introduced, a signal keyed by the token owner, not by DI scope.** The handler that sees
  the refused response runs in the `IHttpClientFactory` handler scope, not the component's, so a
  scoped event service would reach the wrong subscriber. The class keys the signal by the token
  storage that attached the bearer (the same owner [AuthDelegatingHandler](#authdelegatinghandler)
  reports a 401 to), and the subscriber is the listener rendered in that storage's scope
  (`MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:8-11`). `[Rubric §19, State Management]` assesses whether
  cross-component state has one clear owner and lifetime; here the lifetime is the storage instance
  itself: the `ConditionalWeakTable` key means an ended circuit or scope is never kept alive by a
  subscription (`MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:14-15`). `[Rubric §11, Security]` applies because the
  signal is how a step-up demand from the API turns into a prompt instead of a silent failure.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `Subscriptions` (`MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:21`) is the static
    `ConditionalWeakTable<ITokenStorageService, Subscription>`: one subscriber per storage.
  - `Subscribe(ITokenStorageService, Action)` (`MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:27`) null-guards both
    arguments (`MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:29-30`), creates the handle and stores it with
    `AddOrUpdate` (`MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:33`), so a later subscription replaces an earlier one
    (`MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:15-17`), and returns it as an `IDisposable`
    (`MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:34`).
  - `HasSubscriber(owner)` (`MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:40-41`) lets the handler skip all body
    inspection when nothing listens.
  - `Raise(owner)` (`MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:45`) invokes the subscriber when there is one
    (`MultiFactorRequiredSignal.cs:47-50`) and is otherwise a no-op.
- **Why it's built this way**:
  [ADR-051](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/051-client-auth-token-lifecycle.html) makes the token
  storage the unit that owns a session on the client; keying the signal by that same instance keeps
  the 403 path aligned with the 401 renewal path.
- **Where it's used**: `AuthDelegatingHandler.ReportMultiFactorRequiredAsync`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Auth/AuthDelegatingHandler.cs:231`)
  resolves the owner of the refused bearer, returns early unless `HasSubscriber` is true and the
  response is Problem Details (`AuthDelegatingHandler.cs:240-243`), buffers the body, and calls
  `Raise` when it carries the multi-factor-required code (`AuthDelegatingHandler.cs:246-250`).
  [MultiFactorRequiredListener](#multifactorrequiredlistener) subscribes
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Auth/MultiFactorRequiredListener.cs:41`).
  Covered by
  `MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Services/Auth/TwoFactor/MultiFactorRequiredSignalTests.cs`.

### ITwoFactorUIService

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Auth.TwoFactor` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Auth/TwoFactor/ITwoFactorUIService.cs:16` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the client contract for the signed-in account's own two-factor authentication
  against `auth/two-factor`: status, enrollment, recovery codes and turning it off
  (`ITwoFactorUIService.cs:6-9`).
- **Depends on**: [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and the shared response
  contracts [TwoFactorStatusResponse](group-08-auth.md#twofactorstatusresponse),
  [TwoFactorSetupResponse](group-08-auth.md#twofactorsetupresponse) and
  [TwoFactorRecoveryCodesResponse](group-08-auth.md#twofactorrecoverycodesresponse).
- **Concept introduced, a separate interface so existing implementations keep compiling.**
  `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` assesses interface segregation among other things; the remarks say this is a
  separate interface rather than new [IAuthUIService](#iauthuiservice) members precisely so a
  consumer's own `IAuthUIService` implementation keeps compiling (`ITwoFactorUIService.cs:11-12`).
  `[Rubric §24, Forms/Validation/UX Safety]` applies to the write contract: every write is sent once
  and never retried, because enrollment mints a fresh secret per call, a code is accepted once per
  time step, and a regenerated set replaces the previous one (`ITwoFactorUIService.cs:12-14`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `GetStatusAsync` (`ITwoFactorUIService.cs:21`): whether the second factor is on and how many
    recovery codes are left.
  - `BeginEnrollmentAsync` (`ITwoFactorUIService.cs:29`): the API mints a secret and returns the
    shared key and provisioning URI; the factor is not on yet.
  - `ConfirmEnrollmentAsync(code)` (`ITwoFactorUIService.cs:35`): turns the factor on and returns the
    recovery codes, shown once.
  - `RegenerateRecoveryCodesAsync(code)` (`ITwoFactorUIService.cs:41`) and `DisableAsync(code)`
    (`ITwoFactorUIService.cs:47`): both proved with a live authenticator or recovery code.
  - Every member returns `Result`/`Result<T>` carrying the API's own refusal on failure.
- **Where it's used**: implemented by [TwoFactorUIService](#twofactoruiservice) and registered by
  [TwoFactorUIModule](#twofactoruimodule) (`AddTwoFactorUI()`,
  `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/TwoFactor/DependencyInjection.cs:27`); injected by
  [TwoFactorAccount](#twofactoraccount) and [TwoFactorEnrollmentPanel](#twofactorenrollmentpanel). The
  UI gallery supplies a stub (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Gallery/Stubs/StubTwoFactorUIService.cs`).

### LoginRefusals

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Auth.TwoFactor` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Auth/TwoFactor/LoginRefusals.cs:29` · Level 3 · class (internal static)

- **What it is**: the refusal-code classification and notice mapping shared by the sign-in page and
  the two-factor account page, kept out of their code-behind files (`LoginRefusals.cs:24-28`).
- **Depends on**: [LoginRefusal](#loginrefusal), [AuthErrorCodes](group-08-auth.md#autherrorcodes),
  [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and the `LocalizedErrorMessage` extension on it.
  Externals: `IStringLocalizer`.
- **Concept introduced, match the code, never the wording.** `[Rubric §27, Internationalization]`
  assesses whether behavior survives translation; the class comment states the rule: refusals are
  matched on the error code, never on the message, which is localized and may change
  (`LoginRefusals.cs:26-27`). `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` applies because the error code is
  the contract between API and UI.
- **Walkthrough**
  - Constants: `TwoFactorEnabledReason` `"two-factor-enabled"` (`LoginRefusals.cs:32`) and
    `TwoFactorRequiredReason` `"two-factor-required"` (`LoginRefusals.cs:35`), the `reason` query
    values the two-factor page sends to the sign-in page; and `RecentSignInRequiredCode`
    `"Authentication.TwoFactorRecentSignInRequired"` (`LoginRefusals.cs:41`), spelled here because the
    UI references the shared contracts only (`LoginRefusals.cs:37-40`).
  - `Classify(Result)` (`LoginRefusals.cs:46`) returns `Other` unless there is exactly one error
    (list pattern `[var error]`, `LoginRefusals.cs:50-52`), then maps `TwoFactorRequired`,
    `TwoFactorInvalid` and `EmailNotConfirmed` to their steps (`LoginRefusals.cs:55-60`).
  - `HasCode(result, code)` (`LoginRefusals.cs:68-69`) is an ordinal match over every error.
  - `ReasonNoticeKey(reason)` (`LoginRefusals.cs:77`) maps the two reasons to
    `Auth.Login.TwoFactorEnabledNotice` and `Auth.Login.TwoFactorRequiredNotice` and ignores anything
    else (`LoginRefusals.cs:79-81`), so an arbitrary query value cannot select text.
  - `Describe(result, localizer, fallbackKey)` (`LoginRefusals.cs:93`) picks words in three tiers: the
    resource named by a single error code when it exists (`LoginRefusals.cs:98-104`, because the API's
    message is an English sentence), then the API message localized when it can be, then the fallback
    key (`LoginRefusals.cs:107`).
- **Where it's used**: [Login](#login) classifies with it
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Auth/Login.razor.cs:125`);
  [TwoFactorAccount](#twofactoraccount) sends both reasons and uses `HasCode`/`Describe`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Auth/TwoFactor/TwoFactorAccount.razor.cs:225`,
  `TwoFactorAccount.razor.cs:305`, `TwoFactorAccount.razor.cs:356`, `TwoFactorAccount.razor.cs:362`);
  [TwoFactorEnrollmentPanel](#twofactorenrollmentpanel) does the same for enrollment
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Auth/TwoFactor/TwoFactorEnrollmentPanel.razor.cs:101`
  and `TwoFactorEnrollmentPanel.razor.cs:108`).

### TwoFactorUIService

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Auth.TwoFactor` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Auth/TwoFactor/TwoFactorUIService.cs:24` · Level 4 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the HTTP implementation of [ITwoFactorUIService](#itwofactoruiservice) over the
  `auth/two-factor` endpoints (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:10-12`).
- **Depends on**: [AuthenticatedServiceBase](#authenticatedservicebase) (base class),
  [ITokenStorageService](#itokenstorageservice), [HttpResultExecutor](#httpresultexecutor),
  [ProblemDetailsResultReader](group-08-auth.md#problemdetailsresultreader) and
  [TwoFactorCodeRequest](group-08-auth.md#twofactorcoderequest). Externals: `IHttpClientFactory`.
- **Concept introduced**: none new; it follows the authenticated-service shape of
  [MachineClientAdminService](#machineclientadminservice) (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:14-18`): the bearer
  comes from the component's own token storage so a 401 renews the right session, responses are read
  through `ProblemDetailsResultReader` with the API's error codes intact, and transport faults become
  failures through `HttpResultExecutor`. `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` assesses
  whether retries are applied only where safe; here only the status read is retried
  (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:18-19`). `[Rubric §11, Security]` applies too: neither the secret nor a
  recovery code is logged or cached, they live only in the returned value
  (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:19-20`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `Endpoint` is `"auth/two-factor"` (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:29`).
  - `GetStatusAsync` (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:32`) is the only call wrapped in `RetryPolicy.ExecuteAsync`
    (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:37`).
  - `BeginEnrollmentAsync` (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:47`) POSTs `enrollment` with no body
    (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:52-53`).
  - `ConfirmEnrollmentAsync` (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:61-62`) and `RegenerateRecoveryCodesAsync`
    (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:65-66`) share the private `PostCodeAsync` (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:92`),
    which rejects a blank code (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:94`) and posts a trimmed
    `TwoFactorCodeRequest`, reading back the recovery codes (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:100-106`).
  - `DisableAsync` (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:69`) applies the same blank-code guard
    (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:71`) and posts to `disable`, reading a non-generic `Result`
    (`TwoFactorUIService.cs:77-82`).
- **Why it's built this way**:
  [ADR-094](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/094-client-entity-data-access.html) sets the client
  data-access shape the authenticated services share; ADR-051's token-owner tracking is why the
  bearer comes from the injected storage rather than a shared client.
- **Where it's used**: registered as `TryAddScoped<ITwoFactorUIService, TwoFactorUIService>()` by
  `AddTwoFactorUI()`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/TwoFactor/DependencyInjection.cs:27`). Covered by
  `MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Services/Auth/TwoFactor/TwoFactorUIServiceTests.cs`.

### IPublicLinkBuilder

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Navigation` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Navigation/IPublicLinkBuilder.cs:9` · Level 0 · interface

- **What it is**: a one-method abstraction that turns an app-relative path into an absolute, publicly
  shareable URL (`IPublicLinkBuilder.cs:9-13`). It exists so share sheets, copy-link buttons and QR
  payloads produce a URL that still works once it leaves the app.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party. BCL `Uri` and `string`. Implemented by
  [NavigationPublicLinkBuilder](#navigationpubliclinkbuilder) in this package and by
  [MauiPublicLinkBuilder](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#mauipubliclinkbuilder) on the hybrid
  head.
- **Concept introduced, head-agnostic absolute link building.** `[Rubric §18, UI Architecture]`
  assesses whether shared components stay host-agnostic instead of branching on the host they run in,
  and `[Rubric §25, Navigation & Information Architecture]` assesses whether outbound links are built
  from one authority rather than string-concatenated per call site. The doc comment
  (`IPublicLinkBuilder.cs:3-8`) states the problem exactly: web heads can derive a shareable origin
  from the browser, but the MAUI head cannot, because its internal origin is the WebView's virtual
  host. Encoding that virtual origin into a QR code or a shared link would produce a URL nobody
  outside the app can open. One interface with two implementations moves the head-specific knowledge
  to the composition root and lets the pages stay identical on every head.
- **Walkthrough**
  - A single member, `Uri BuildAbsolute(string relativePath)` (`IPublicLinkBuilder.cs:13`). It returns
    a `Uri` rather than a `string`, so callers that need text do the `ToString()` themselves, and the
    doc comment gives `/sessions/42` as the shape of the argument (`IPublicLinkBuilder.cs:11`).
  - The default binding resolves the path against `NavigationManager.BaseUri`
    (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Navigation/NavigationPublicLinkBuilder.cs:25`),
    after rejecting a blank path (`NavigationPublicLinkBuilder.cs:23`).
  - The hybrid binding resolves against the `PublicSite:BaseUrl` key pinned in the head's embedded
    configuration
    (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Maui/Services/MauiPublicLinkBuilder.cs:17` and
    `MauiPublicLinkBuilder.cs:28-32`), and throws `InvalidOperationException` at construction when the
    key is missing, so a misconfigured head fails at startup instead of shipping unusable links.
- **Why it's built this way**: the default is registered with `TryAddScoped`
  (`DependencyInjection.cs:161`) and the comment above it (`DependencyInjection.cs:157-160`) records
  the override rule: the hybrid head calls `AddCommonMauiPublicLinkBuilder()` after `AddUIShared`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Maui/DependencyInjection.cs:152-153`, invoked at
  `MMCA.ADC/Source/Hosts/UI/MMCA.ADC.UI/MauiProgram.cs:156`) and the last registration wins. That is
  the same head-override composition convention
  [ADR-042](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/042-device-capability-abstraction.html) establishes
  for the device capability layer.
- **Where it's used**: the shared `SharePageButton` component
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Sharing/SharePageButton.razor:4` and
  `SharePageButton.razor:43`), the shared `QrCodeButton` component (`QrCodeButton.razor:1` and
  `QrCodeButton.razor:79`), and app pages such as ADC's speaker QR page
  (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Speakers/SpeakerQr.razor.cs:26` and
  `SpeakerQr.razor.cs:62`). A bUnit test pins the default registration to the browser-origin builder
  (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Services/Navigation/NavigationPublicLinkBuilderTests.cs:59`).

### BackNavigationResult
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Navigation` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Navigation/MauiBackNavigationBridge.cs:19` · Level 0 · record (sealed)

- **What it is**: the outcome of a hardware-back or WebView-back attempt routed through
  [MauiBackNavigationBridge](#mauibacknavigationbridge): whether the WebView consumed the gesture, and
  whether the WebView is sitting at the root of its history stack.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party. It is a two-field positional record produced and consumed by
  [MauiBackNavigationBridge](#mauibacknavigationbridge).
- **Concept introduced, the interop return contract.** This record is also the wire shape of a single
  JS interop call: `nav-interop.js`'s `tryGoBack()` returns an object that deserializes straight into
  it (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Navigation/MauiBackNavigationBridge.cs:48`),
  so the C# type and the JS return value are one contract.
- **Walkthrough**: `public sealed record BackNavigationResult(bool Handled, bool AtRoot)`
  (`MauiBackNavigationBridge.cs:19`). `Handled` is `true` when the WebView's history stack contained a
  previous entry and `history.back()` fired (`MauiBackNavigationBridge.cs:9-13`); `AtRoot` is `true`
  when no previous entry exists, and the doc comment records that MAUI hosts typically exit the app on
  Android when that is reported (`MauiBackNavigationBridge.cs:14-18`).
- **Why it's built this way**: a `sealed record` buys structural equality and positional
  deconstruction for free, and it is the smallest thing that can carry the two facts the native host
  needs. Modeling the answer as data (rather than throwing, or mutating shared state) keeps the interop
  call pure and trivially testable.
- **Where it's used**: returned by
  [MauiBackNavigationBridge](#mauibacknavigationbridge)`.HandleBackPressedAsync`; consumed by MAUI host
  `ContentPage.OnBackButtonPressed` handlers.

### ReturnUrlProtector
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Navigation` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Navigation/ReturnUrlProtector.cs:9` · Level 0 · class (static)

- **What it is**: a pure sanitizer for `returnUrl` query parameters: it accepts only same-origin
  relative paths and replaces anything else with a safe fallback, closing the open-redirect hole in
  post-login and post-action redirects.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party; `System.Uri` (BCL) supplies the final relative-URI parse guard.
- **Concept introduced, open-redirect defense.** `[Rubric §26, Front-End Security]` assesses whether
  user-controlled navigation targets are validated before use. An open redirect lets an attacker craft
  `/login?returnUrl=https://evil.com` so the victim lands on an attacker site *after* authenticating, a
  classic phishing amplifier. `Sanitize` rejects every off-host form rather than trying to enumerate
  attacks, and the ordered guards read as a documented threat model.
- **Walkthrough**: `Sanitize(string? candidate, string fallback = "/")` (`ReturnUrlProtector.cs:18`)
  runs a sequence of cheap, regex-free checks (a regex here would invite ReDoS), each returning
  `fallback` on failure:
  - null or empty (lines 20-23);
  - must start with `/`, which rules out scheme-prefixed absolutes such as `http://` and
    `javascript:` (lines 25-30);
  - the second character must not be `/` or `\`, which browsers read as the start of an authority
    component and would send the user off-host (lines 32-37);
  - no backslash anywhere, since some browsers normalize `\` to `/` (the source names
    `"/\\evil.com"` becoming `//evil.com` in Chrome, lines 39-44);
  - no control characters, which are header-injection, response-splitting and cookie-smuggling
    vectors (lines 46-51);
  - and finally it must parse as a well-formed relative URI (`Uri.TryCreate(..., UriKind.Relative)`,
    lines 53-57).
  Only a candidate that survives all six is returned unchanged (line 59).
- **Why it's built this way**: a static pure function whose only input is the candidate is trivially
  unit-testable across every attack vector, and calling it centrally means no page hand-rolls its own
  redirect validation.
- **Where it's used**: login and post-authentication redirects sanitize the `returnUrl` they read from
  the query string; [NavigationHistoryService](#navigationhistoryservice)`.GoBackAsync` also runs its
  fallback path through it (`NavigationHistoryService.cs:82`), so even the "safe" branch cannot be
  turned into a redirect vector.

### AuthEmailPrefill
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Navigation` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Navigation/AuthEmailPrefill.cs:11` · Level 0 · class (internal, static)

- **What it is**: a two-method helper that hands an email address from one shared auth page to the
  next through the navigation's history state rather than the URL, so a page can open with the address
  already typed (`AuthEmailPrefill.cs:5-10`).
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party. `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.NavigationManager` and
  `NavigationOptions` (ASP.NET Core Blazor, `AuthEmailPrefill.cs:1`).
- **Concept introduced, history state as a private side channel.** `[Rubric §26, Front-End Security]`
  assesses whether sensitive values stay out of places they leak from. A query string such as
  `/login?email=...` is written into the address bar, browser history, server request logs and the
  `Referer` header of any outbound request; `NavigationOptions.HistoryEntryState` travels with the
  history entry and appears in none of those, which is exactly the reason the class doc gives
  (`AuthEmailPrefill.cs:6-7`). `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]` reads the other side: the
  user is not asked to retype an address the app already holds.
- **Walkthrough**
  - Two private prefixes tag the state string (`AuthEmailPrefill.cs:13-14`):
    `"mmca-auth:existing-account:"` and `"mmca-auth:prefill:"`. The prefix carries one extra bit, whether
    the address was just refused because it already holds an account.
  - `NavigateWithEmail(navigation, path, email, existingAccount = false)` (`AuthEmailPrefill.cs:23-27`)
    calls `NavigateTo(path, new NavigationOptions { HistoryEntryState = prefix + email })`.
  - `Read(navigation, out bool existingAccount)` (`AuthEmailPrefill.cs:33-52`) reads
    `navigation.HistoryEntryState`, returns `null` when there is none (`:38-41`), sets `existingAccount`
    and strips the prefix when the existing-account tag matches (`:43-47`), strips the plain prefix
    otherwise (`:49-51`), and returns `null` for any state it did not write. Both comparisons are
    `StringComparison.Ordinal`. `NonEmpty` (`:54`) turns a blank remainder into `null`, so a page never
    prefills an empty string over its own default.
- **Why it's built this way**: the prefix check means a history entry written by some other code is
  ignored rather than misread as an address, and keeping the class `internal` holds the convention to
  the shared auth pages that read and write it. No ADR records the choice; the rationale is the class
  doc (`AuthEmailPrefill.cs:5-10`).
- **Where it's used**: [Register](#register) lands a duplicate address on sign-in with
  `existingAccount: true` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Auth/Register.razor:268`)
  and sends the pending address to sign-in
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Auth/Register.razor.cs:79`); [Login](#login)
  reads it (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Auth/Login.razor.cs:182`) and hands
  the typed address to `/forgot-password` (`Login.razor.cs:211`), which reads it back
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Auth/ForgotPassword.razor:82`). bUnit tests
  drive the round trip
  (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Pages/Auth/SignInLinks/LoginSignInLinkTests.cs:47`,
  `MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Pages/Auth/RegistrationPending/RegisterPendingTests.cs:83`).
- **Caveats**: history state lives only on the history entry; a fresh URL typed or opened in a new tab
  carries no state, and the page falls back to an empty field.

### IForbiddenReExecutionDetector
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Navigation` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Navigation/IForbiddenReExecutionDetector.cs:17` · Level 0 · interface

- **What it is**: a one-property contract that answers whether the page being rendered is a
  status-code re-execution of a request the server already refused with 403 Forbidden
  (`IForbiddenReExecutionDetector.cs:3-5`, `:23`).
- **Depends on**: nothing. Implemented by [NoForbiddenReExecutionDetector](#noforbiddenreexecutiondetector)
  in this package and by
  [HttpContextForbiddenReExecutionDetector](#httpcontextforbiddenreexecutiondetector) in
  `MMCA.Common.UI.Web`.
- **Concept introduced, a server-only question behind a head-neutral contract.** `[Rubric §18, UI
  Architecture & Component Design]` assesses whether shared components stay host-agnostic. Hosts
  re-execute error statuses to `/not-found` (`UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("/not-found")`), so a
  full page load refused with 403 also lands on the not-found page with the original status still on
  the response (`IForbiddenReExecutionDetector.cs:7-10`). Only a server render can read that response,
  and `MMCA.Common.UI` must stay free of server types so it runs on Blazor WebAssembly (`:10-11`), so
  the question is asked through this interface and answered per head. `[Rubric §25, Navigation,
  Routing & Information Architecture]` reads the result: a signed-in user who lacks a permission sees
  Access Denied, not a misleading Page Not Found.
- **Walkthrough**: a single getter, `bool IsForbiddenReExecution { get; }`
  (`IForbiddenReExecutionDetector.cs:23`), documented to answer `false` whenever there is no request to
  read (`:19-22`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the same head-override composition used across the UI layer.
  `AddUIShared` registers the always-false default with `TryAddSingleton`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:247-250`), and the Blazor Web
  host's `AddMmcaBlazorWebHost` replaces it with the request-reading one
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/Hosting/BlazorWebHostExtensions.cs:139`), which
  compares `HttpContext.Response.StatusCode` to 403
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/Services/HttpContextForbiddenReExecutionDetector.cs:31-32`).
- **Where it's used**: injected by the shared `NotFound` page
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/NotFound.razor:6`), which renders the
  `Forbidden` view when it answers `true` and the not-found content otherwise (`NotFound.razor:16-28`).
  `MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Pages/NotFoundTests.cs` covers both branches, and
  `HttpContextForbiddenReExecutionDetectorTests` covers the server implementation.

### InAppDiagnosticsOptions
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Diagnostics` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Diagnostics/InAppDiagnosticsOptions.cs:10` · Level 0 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the options for the in-app diagnostics log: how many entries the in-memory buffer
  keeps and the lowest level it records (`InAppDiagnosticsOptions.cs:7-9`).
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party. `System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.RangeAttribute` and
  `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LogLevel`.
- **Concept introduced**: none new; a plain options class validated without reflection by
  [InAppDiagnosticsOptionsValidator](#inappdiagnosticsoptionsvalidator), the same shape as
  [ApiSettings](#apisettings) and [ApiSettingsValidator](#apisettingsvalidator).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `DefaultCapacity = 500` (`InAppDiagnosticsOptions.cs:13`).
  - `Capacity` (`:19-20`), `[Range(1, 100_000)]`, defaulting to `DefaultCapacity`; when the buffer is
    full each new entry drops the oldest (`:15-18`).
  - `MinimumLevel` (`:26`), defaulting to `LogLevel.Information`, so Debug and Trace never reach the
    buffer (`:22-25`).
- **Why it's built this way**: compiled-in defaults let a host call `AddInAppDiagnostics()` with no
  configuration at all, and the range bound keeps a mistyped capacity from allocating an oversized
  array.
- **Where it's used**: configured through the optional callback of
  [DependencyInjection](#dependencyinjection-2)`.AddInAppDiagnostics`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Diagnostics/DependencyInjection.cs:27-33`);
  read by [InAppLogBuffer](#inapplogbuffer) (capacity) and [InAppLoggerProvider](#inapploggerprovider)
  (minimum level).

### InAppLogEntry
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Diagnostics` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Diagnostics/InAppLogEntry.cs:15` · Level 0 · record (sealed, positional)

- **What it is**: one log record held by [InAppLogBuffer](#inapplogbuffer): timestamp, level,
  category, formatted message and an optional exception description (`InAppLogEntry.cs:15-20`).
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party. `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LogLevel`, BCL `DateTimeOffset`
  and `CultureInfo`.
- **Concept introduced**: none; a positional record used as an immutable value.
- **Walkthrough**: the five positional members (`InAppLogEntry.cs:15-20`), where `Exception` is a
  `string?` rather than an `Exception` object, so the buffer holds no live exception graph. The
  `ToString()` override (`:27-33`) is the text that is copied and shared (`:22-26`): an
  invariant-culture line of the UTC timestamp as `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.fff` with a `Z` suffix, the level
  in brackets, the category and the message (`:29-31`), plus a second indented line carrying the
  exception when there is one (`:32`).
- **Why it's built this way**: formatting with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` and UTC keeps a log a
  user shares readable by whoever receives it, whatever the device locale or time zone.
- **Where it's used**: produced by the private [InAppLogger](#inapplogger), stored by
  [InAppLogBuffer](#inapplogbuffer), and rendered by the `InAppDiagnosticsLog` component.

### NavigationPublicLinkBuilder
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Navigation` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Navigation/NavigationPublicLinkBuilder.cs:11` · Level 1 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: the default [IPublicLinkBuilder](#ipubliclinkbuilder). It turns an app-relative route
  such as `sessions/42` into an absolute URL by resolving it against the origin the browser is
  currently served from, which is what a share sheet, a copy-link button or a QR payload needs.
- **Depends on**: [IPublicLinkBuilder](#ipubliclinkbuilder) (the contract it implements,
  `NavigationPublicLinkBuilder.cs:11`); `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.NavigationManager` (ASP.NET
  Core Blazor, `NavigationPublicLinkBuilder.cs:1,13`) for the origin. Nothing else: no HTTP, no
  configuration, no JS interop.
- **Concept introduced, the origin a link is built from is a per-head decision, not a per-page one.**
  `[Rubric §25, Navigation, Routing & Information Architecture]` assesses whether routes and the URLs
  built from them are modelled once rather than reconstructed ad hoc at each call site. A page that
  wants to share itself has two candidate origins available, and only one of them is right: the
  in-process origin the component is rendering under, and the public web origin a recipient can open.
  On the Server and WebAssembly heads those coincide, so `NavigationManager.BaseUri` is the correct
  answer and this class is a two-line adapter over it. On the MAUI Blazor Hybrid head they do not: the
  WebView serves the app from an internal virtual host, so an absolute URL built from `BaseUri` there
  would be unopenable anywhere else (the class comment records exactly this at lines 5-10). Hoisting
  the decision behind an interface is what lets the shared `SharePageButton` and `QrCodeButton` stay
  head-agnostic (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Sharing/SharePageButton.razor:4`,
  `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Sharing/QrCodeButton.razor:1`).
  `[Rubric §18, UI Architecture & Component Design]` reads the same choice from the component side:
  the shared components inject a contract, never a `NavigationManager`.
- **Walkthrough**
  - One readonly field, `_navigationManager` (line 13), assigned by an expression-bodied constructor
    (lines 17-18). The class is `sealed` and holds no other state, so a scoped instance costs a
    reference.
  - `BuildAbsolute(string relativePath)` (line 21) rejects a blank path outright with
    `ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace` (line 23): an empty share link is a caller bug, not a
    condition to render, and this is the one place cheap enough to catch it.
  - The build itself is one expression (line 25):
    `new Uri(new Uri(_navigationManager.BaseUri, UriKind.Absolute), relativePath)`. The inner `Uri`
    forces the base to be parsed as absolute, and the outer resolution applies standard URI reference
    resolution to the path.
  - The behavior callers rely on is pinned rather than assumed:
    [NavigationPublicLinkBuilderTests](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup)
    asserts that `"/sessions/42"` and `"sessions/42"` both resolve to `http://localhost/sessions/42`
    against the bUnit origin
    (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Services/Navigation/NavigationPublicLinkBuilderTests.cs:21-25`),
    that a query string survives (`:27-29`), and that a blank path throws (`:31-41`).
- **Why it's built this way**: `AddUIShared` registers this implementation with `TryAddScoped`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:237`), so every head gets a
  working builder without opting in, and the one head that must differ replaces it afterwards:
  `AddCommonMauiPublicLinkBuilder()` registers
  [MauiPublicLinkBuilder](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#mauipubliclinkbuilder) over the
  configured public site URL
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Maui/DependencyInjection.cs:153`). The registration
  shape is itself asserted, implementation type and lifetime, so a refactor that changes the default is
  a red test rather than a silently wrong share link (`NavigationPublicLinkBuilderTests.cs:43-62`).
- **Where it's used**: injected by the framework's share affordances, `SharePageButton` and
  `QrCodeButton`, and by ADC's [SpeakerQr](group-21-conference-ui.md#speakerqr) page, which encodes the
  absolute public URL into the badge QR rather than the WebView origin
  (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Speakers/SpeakerQr.razor.cs:26`).
  The bUnit harnesses in both repos register it explicitly so component tests exercise the real builder
  (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/BunitTestBase.cs:42`,
  `MMCA.ADC/Tests/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI.Tests/BunitTestBase.cs:35`).
- **Caveats**: `BuildAbsolute` performs no allow-list check on `relativePath`, and nothing in the class
  restricts the result to the app's own origin, so a path value that came from user input should be
  sanitized upstream.

### MauiBackNavigationBridge
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Navigation` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Navigation/MauiBackNavigationBridge.cs:28` · Level 1 · class (static)

- **What it is**: a static bridge that routes a native MAUI back gesture (Android hardware back, iOS
  swipe) into the BlazorWebView's internal history stack, so pressing back inside a hybrid app behaves
  like a web back rather than tearing down the page.
- **Depends on**: [BackNavigationResult](#backnavigationresult) (its return type);
  `Microsoft.JSInterop` (`IJSRuntime`, `IJSObjectReference`, `JSDisconnectedException`, `JSException`)
  and the `nav-interop.js` module shipped as static web assets of this package.
- **Concept introduced, MAUI-to-WebView interop.** `[Rubric §22, Responsive & Cross-Browser]` extends
  to hybrid hosts here: the same Blazor UI runs inside a MAUI WebView, and native chrome events must be
  reconciled with web navigation. The class doc states the required call site precisely, from
  `ContentPage.OnBackButtonPressed` via `BlazorWebView.TryDispatchAsync`, so the call runs on the
  renderer thread with access to the WebView's `IJSRuntime` (`MauiBackNavigationBridge.cs:21-27`).
- **Walkthrough**: `HandleBackPressedAsync(IJSRuntime js)` (line 38) null-checks the runtime
  (`ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull`, line 40), dynamically imports
  `./_content/MMCA.Common.UI/nav-interop.js` (`ModulePath`, line 30) into an `await using` module
  reference (line 47) and invokes its `tryGoBack()` helper, deserializing the answer into a
  [BackNavigationResult](#backnavigationresult) (lines 48-49). The module reference is disposed on
  every call: the class is static, so nothing else owns it, and re-importing on each back press without
  disposing would leak one JS object reference per press (comment at lines 44-46). Three interop
  failure modes are caught explicitly and collapse to the same safe value
  `new BackNavigationResult(Handled: false, AtRoot: true)`: `InvalidOperationException` when Blazor is
  not yet hydrated (lines 51-55), `JSDisconnectedException` (lines 56-59, which also covers a dispose
  on a torn-down circuit), and `JSException` (lines 60-63). A not-yet-ready WebView therefore reports
  "at root, not handled" and the host falls back to its default back behavior.
- **Why it's built this way**: a static helper with no state fits a one-shot interop call, and
  returning a data record instead of throwing keeps the native handler branch-free. Because it holds no
  state, it also cannot cache the imported module, which is why each call owns and disposes its own
  reference. Collapsing the three JS exception types into one safe default means an unhydrated or
  disconnected circuit never crashes the native back button.
- **Where it's used**: the MAUI host base page in `MMCA.Common.UI.Maui`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Maui/MainPageBase.cs:255`) calls it from its
  `OnBackButtonPressed` override (`MainPageBase.cs:216`); the returned [BackNavigationResult](#backnavigationresult) tells the host
  whether to exit the app.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the `nav-interop.js` `tryGoBack()` implementation and the
  `MainPageBase` dispatch logic live outside this unit; only the C# side of the bridge is visible here.

### NavigationHistoryService
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Navigation` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Navigation/NavigationHistoryService.cs:12` · Level 1 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: a per-circuit service that bridges Blazor's `NavigationManager` with the browser
  history API, so a "Back" button can perform a real `history.back()` when an in-history entry exists
  and fall back to an explicit route otherwise.
- **Depends on**: [ReturnUrlProtector](#returnurlprotector) (sanitizes the fallback) and
  [LazyJsModule](#lazyjsmodule) (the shared single-flight JS module importer, held as `_module`,
  `NavigationHistoryService.cs:16`); `NavigationManager` and `IJSRuntime` arrive through the primary
  constructor (line 12). Implements `IAsyncDisposable`.
- **Concept introduced, honoring real browser history.** `[Rubric §25, Navigation, Routing &
  Information Architecture]` assesses predictable, source-aware navigation. A hard-coded "back to list"
  link ignores where the user actually came from; this service instead asks the browser whether a
  previous entry exists and navigates to it, falling back to a route only when it does not
  (`NavigationHistoryService.cs:50-54`). `[Rubric §26, Front-End Security]` applies to the fallback:
  it is sanitized rather than trusted (line 82).
- **Walkthrough**:
  - `ModulePath` (line 14) names `./_content/MMCA.Common.UI/nav-interop.js`, the same module the MAUI
    bridge imports; `_module` wraps it in a [LazyJsModule](#lazyjsmodule) (line 16) so concurrent
    callers share one import.
  - `CanGoBackAsync()` (lines 23-48) resolves the module, returns `false` when it is unavailable
    (lines 28-31), then invokes `historyLength` and reports `length > 1` (lines 33-34). Interop
    failures during SSR prerender or after a disconnect are swallowed as `false`
    (`InvalidOperationException`, `JSDisconnectedException`, `JSException`, lines 36-47).
  - `GoBackAsync(string fallback = "/")` (lines 55-83) calls `historyBack` when history is available
    and returns (lines 57-66); every interop failure falls through the three catch blocks
    (lines 68-79) to the single exit at line 82,
    `navigation.NavigateTo(ReturnUrlProtector.Sanitize(fallback))`. The method therefore always ends in
    a navigation.
  - `GetModuleAsync()` (lines 85-99) delegates to `_module.GetOrImportAsync()` and turns a prerender or
    disconnect failure into `null` rather than an exception.
  - `DisposeAsync()` (line 102) forwards to the module wrapper, releasing the imported JS reference
    with the circuit.
- **Why it's built this way**: sealed and scoped per circuit, because the cached JS module reference
  and history semantics are per-connection. Delegating the import to [LazyJsModule](#lazyjsmodule)
  removes a real bug class: an unguarded `_module ??= await import(...)` lets two concurrent callers
  each start an import and leaks the loser's reference
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/LazyJsModule.cs:5-13`). Routing the
  fallback through [ReturnUrlProtector](#returnurlprotector) means even the safe branch cannot be
  turned into a redirect vector, and the layered exception handling guarantees `GoBackAsync` never
  strands the user.
- **Where it's used**: injected into detail-page "Back" buttons; the same `nav-interop.js` primitives
  back the MAUI hardware-back path through
  [MauiBackNavigationBridge](#mauibacknavigationbridge).

### InAppLogBuffer
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Diagnostics` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Diagnostics/InAppLogBuffer.cs:11` · Level 3 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: a fixed-size, thread-safe ring buffer of [InAppLogEntry](#inapplogentry) records: the
  in-memory store behind the in-app diagnostics log.
- **Depends on**: [InAppLogEntry](#inapplogentry), [InAppDiagnosticsOptions](#inappdiagnosticsoptions)
  (through `IOptions<T>`); BCL `System.Threading.Lock`.
- **Concept introduced, a bounded ring buffer as a crash-free log sink.** `[Rubric §13, Observability &
  Operability]` assesses whether a running system can be diagnosed. A MAUI store build has no console
  and no attached debugger, so its logs otherwise go nowhere
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Diagnostics/DependencyInjection.cs:21-23`);
  this buffer keeps the most recent entries where the user can see them. A ring of fixed capacity is
  the right shape for that: memory is allocated once and never grows, however long the app runs, and
  the oldest entries are the ones worth losing.
- **Walkthrough**
  - Fields (`InAppLogBuffer.cs:13-16`): a `Lock` gate, the entry array, `_next` (the write index) and
    `_count`.
  - The constructor (`:20-26`) reads `Capacity` from options, rejects anything below 1 with
    `ArgumentOutOfRangeException.ThrowIfLessThan` (`:24`) and allocates the array once.
  - `Capacity` (`:29`) is the array length; `Count` (`:32-41`) reads `_count` under the lock.
  - `Add` (`:45-58`) writes at `_next`, advances it modulo the length, and increments `_count` only
    until the buffer is full (`:51-57`), so a full buffer overwrites its oldest slot.
  - `Snapshot()` (`:62-75`) copies the held entries into a new array, oldest first, starting at
    `(_next - _count + length) % length` (`:67`), so callers never see the live array.
  - `Clear()` (`:78-86`) wipes the array and resets both counters; `ToText()` (`:90`) joins the snapshot
    with `Environment.NewLine`, using each entry's `ToString()`.
- **Why it's built this way**: every member takes the same lock, so the logger can write from any
  thread while the UI takes a snapshot. Returning a copy keeps rendering free of the lock after the
  snapshot is taken.
- **Where it's used**: written by [InAppLoggerProvider](#inapploggerprovider), registered as a singleton
  by `AddInAppDiagnostics`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Diagnostics/DependencyInjection.cs:41`), and
  injected by the shared `InAppDiagnosticsLog` component
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Diagnostics/InAppDiagnosticsLog.razor:5`),
  which ADC's MAUI head shows on its device settings page
  (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Hosts/UI/MMCA.ADC.UI/Pages/DeviceSettings.razor:50`).
- **Caveats**: the buffer is process memory only; it is lost when the app exits, and nothing persists
  or uploads it unless the user copies or shares the text.

### InAppLogger
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Diagnostics` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Diagnostics/InAppLoggerProvider.cs:44` · Level 4 · class (private, sealed, nested in InAppLoggerProvider)

- **What it is**: the `ILogger` that [InAppLoggerProvider](#inapploggerprovider) hands out per category;
  it turns each enabled log call into an [InAppLogEntry](#inapplogentry) in the shared
  [InAppLogBuffer](#inapplogbuffer).
- **Depends on**: its enclosing [InAppLoggerProvider](#inapploggerprovider) (buffer, clock and minimum
  level through the primary constructor, `InAppLoggerProvider.cs:44`), [InAppLogEntry](#inapplogentry);
  `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILogger`.
- **Concept introduced**: none beyond the provider's; see [InAppLoggerProvider](#inapploggerprovider).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `BeginScope` returns `null` (`InAppLoggerProvider.cs:46-47`): scopes are not recorded.
  - `IsEnabled` (`:49-50`) is true for any level other than `None` at or above the configured minimum.
  - `Log` (`:52-72`) null-checks the formatter, returns early when the level is disabled (`:61-64`), and
    adds an entry stamped with `TimeProvider.GetUtcNow()`, the category, the formatted message and,
    when present, a described exception (`:66-71`).
  - `DescribeException` (`:74-88`) walks the `InnerException` chain, writing each type's full name and
    message joined by `" ---> "` (`:77-85`). The stack trace is not kept.
- **Why it's built this way**: the exception is flattened to a string so the buffer holds no exception
  objects (and their captured state) alive, and the clock is injected so tests can assert timestamps.
- **Where it's used**: only through `InAppLoggerProvider.CreateLogger` (`InAppLoggerProvider.cs:36`);
  it has no other reference.

### InAppLoggerProvider
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Diagnostics` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Diagnostics/InAppLoggerProvider.cs:14` · Level 4 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: an `ILoggerProvider` that records log entries at or above
  `InAppDiagnosticsOptions.MinimumLevel` into the in-memory [InAppLogBuffer](#inapplogbuffer); nothing is
  written to disk or sent anywhere (`InAppLoggerProvider.cs:8-12`).
- **Depends on**: [InAppLogBuffer](#inapplogbuffer), [InAppDiagnosticsOptions](#inappdiagnosticsoptions),
  [InAppLogger](#inapplogger) (nested), [InAppLogEntry](#inapplogentry); BCL `TimeProvider`,
  `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging` and `Microsoft.Extensions.Options`.
- **Concept introduced, a logging provider as a pluggable sink.** `[Rubric §13, Observability &
  Operability]` assesses whether diagnostics reach someone who can act on them. The logger factory fans
  every `ILogger` call out to each registered `ILoggerProvider`, so adding this provider captures the
  output of every existing log call on the head with no change at a call site.
  `[Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance]` applies to the destination: the log never leaves
  the process unless the user copies or shares it
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Diagnostics/DependencyInjection.cs:23-24`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - Fields (`InAppLoggerProvider.cs:16-18`): the buffer, the clock and the minimum level.
  - The constructor (`:24-33`) null-checks its three arguments and reads `MinimumLevel` once (`:32`).
  - `CreateLogger(categoryName)` (`:36`) returns a new [InAppLogger](#inapplogger) bound to this
    provider and the category.
  - `Dispose()` (`:39-42`) releases nothing: the buffer is a DI singleton of its own and outlives the
    provider (`:41`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the buffer is a separate singleton so the UI can inject it directly
  without going through logging, and the minimum level is captured at construction, so a change needs
  a restart rather than a live reload.
- **Where it's used**: registered by `AddInAppDiagnostics` with `TryAddEnumerable`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Diagnostics/DependencyInjection.cs:46`);
  covered by `MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Services/Diagnostics/InAppLoggerProviderTests.cs`.

### DependencyInjection
> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Diagnostics` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Diagnostics/DependencyInjection.cs:13` · Level 5 · class (static, with one `extension(IServiceCollection)` block)

- **What it is**: the opt-in registration for the in-app diagnostics log, one method,
  `AddInAppDiagnostics` (`DependencyInjection.cs:27`). This is the `Services.Diagnostics` class of that
  name, separate from the `MMCA.Common.UI` composition root that holds `AddUIShared`.

  [InAppDiagnosticsOptionsValidator](#inappdiagnosticsoptionsvalidator),
