  covers presenting data the way the user will read it. The viewer's time zone is only readable once JS
  interop is available, so the component resolves it after the first render and re-renders once it is
  known (`UserSessionsTable.razor.cs:42-49`); until then the instants format on the default zone.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `Sessions` is an `[EditorRequired]` parameter defaulting to an empty list
    (`UserSessionsTable.razor.cs:27-29`).
  - `OnAfterRenderAsync` runs the zone lookup on first render only, skips it once disposed, and calls
    `StateHasChanged` when the lookup resolved a zone (`UserSessionsTable.razor.cs:42-49`).
  - Row helpers: `DescribeDevice` passes the session's recorded `Device` and its `UserAgent` to
    `UserAgentSummary.Describe` (`:69`), `DescribeIpAddress` falls back to the localized
    `Auth.Sessions.IpUnknown` text when the address is blank (`:71-72`), and `FormatInstant` calls
    `ViewerTime.Format` (`:74`).
  - Disposal: the component implements `IDisposable` with the usual protected `Dispose(bool)`; it cancels
    and disposes the `CancellationTokenSource` that bounds the zone lookup (`:35-67`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the table owns no data fetching, so the same component serves any page that
  holds a session list, and the cancel-on-dispose token keeps a navigation away from leaving the zone
  lookup running. Its history counterpart [SignInHistoryTable](#signinhistorytable) follows the same
  shape and the same device description.
- **Where it's used**: ADC's user detail page
  (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.UI/Pages/Users/UserDetail/UserDetail.razor:112`), and
  pinned by `UserSessionsTableTests`
  (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Components/Auth/UserSessionsTableTests.cs`) and ADC's
  `UserDetailTests`.

### FieldRefusal

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Components.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Auth/ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:198` · Level 3 · record struct (private, nested in [ChangePasswordCard](#changepasswordcard))

- **What it is**: a server message for one form field, held against the exact value it was raised for, so
  it clears itself the moment the user edits that field (doc comment, `ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:194-197`).
- **Depends on**: `Result` ([Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result)) and its `Errors`
  (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:202`); the target and code of each error.
- **Concept introduced, a refusal bound to a value.** `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]`
  assesses whether a server rejection is shown where the user can act on it. Holding the value beside the
  message means no timer or event is needed to dismiss a stale message: `MessageFor` compares the field's
  current value to the stored one and returns `null` once they differ.
- **Walkthrough**
  - The positional record struct carries `Value` and `Message` (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:198`); the
    `default` instance carries neither, so an unset refusal never matches.
  - `From(result, field, value, matchCode)` picks the first error whose target names the field or whose
    code equals `matchCode`, and returns `default` when there is none or its message is blank
    (`:200-209`).
  - `MessageFor(value)` returns the message only on an ordinal match with the stored value (`:211-212`).
  - `TargetsField` returns false for an empty target, then compares the last dotted segment of the
    error target to the field name, case-insensitively (`:216-225`). The segment start is found with
    `AsSpan().LastIndexOf('.')` (`:223`). The comment (`:214-215`) records why only the last segment
    counts: a validator over the request yields `NewPassword`, one over the command yields
    `Request.NewPassword`, in either casing once it crossed the wire.
- **Why it's built this way**: it is a `readonly record struct`, so the two fields on the card
  (`_currentPasswordRefusal`, `_newPasswordRefusal`, `ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:43-44`) cost no
  allocation and compare by value.
- **Where it's used**: only [ChangePasswordCard](#changepasswordcard): `ShowFieldRefusalsAsync` builds the
  two refusals (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:185-186`) and the validators read them (`:103`, `:121`).

### MobileInfiniteScrollList<TItem>

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Components.Lists` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Lists/MobileInfiniteScrollList.razor.cs:20` · Level 3 · class (generic partial component)

- **What it is**: the mobile card list every list page falls back to on a narrow viewport. It owns the whole loop: an IntersectionObserver sentinel that asks for the next page, an accumulated item list rendered through a caller-supplied card template (with optional per-card actions beside it), a rendered-item cap that bounds DOM growth, generation-guarded supersession of in-flight fetches, and localized load-failure handling with a Retry button.
- **Depends on**: [`Result`](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and its generic form (the fetch delegate's return type), [`SharedResource`](#sharedresource) through `IStringLocalizer<SharedResource>`, [`ResultUiExtensions.LocalizedErrorMessage`](#resultuiextensions), the `EmptyState` component, the `ClickableCard` component each row's card is wrapped in, and, through [`InfiniteScrollObserver<TOwner>`](#infinitescrollobservertowner), the shared `_content/MMCA.Common.UI/infinite-scroll.js` module it shares with [`InfiniteScrollSentinel`](#infinitescrollsentinel). Externals: `IJSRuntime`, `DotNetObjectReference`, `CancellationTokenSource`, MudBlazor primitives.
- **Concept introduced, generation-guarded supersession.** `[Rubric §19, State Management]` (assesses whether concurrent updates to client state have a defined winner) and `[Rubric §23, Front-End Performance]`. The hard problem in an infinite list is not fetching, it is what happens when the user changes the filter while a fetch is in flight. Cancellation alone is not enough: the fetch delegate is consumer-supplied and may ignore its `CancellationToken` entirely, so a superseded call can still complete successfully and try to append rows to a list that was cleared. The answer here is a monotonically increasing `_generation` counter (line 72). A load snapshots it before awaiting (line 166) and discards its results if the value moved while it waited (line 182). The token cancellation is still issued (it stops work that *does* honor it), but the generation, not the token, is authoritative (comment, lines 179-181). The second half of the pattern is that **the page counter is computed, not committed**: `targetPage = _currentPage + 1` (line 173) and `_currentPage` only advances on a successful, non-superseded completion (line 197), so a cancelled, failed or superseded fetch leaves nothing to compensate back and no page is ever re-requested (comment, lines 170-172).
- **Concept introduced, card actions beside the clickable area, not inside it.** `[Rubric §21, Accessibility]` assesses whether interactive controls are nested inside other interactive controls. `CardActionsTemplate` (lines 29-37) renders a row's delete or edit buttons beside the card body rather than inside the element that carries the card's button role, so a clickable card that also holds actions is not axe nested-interactive and a tap on an action does not raise `OnCardClick`.
- **Walkthrough**:
  - Injected services (lines 22-23: `IJSRuntime` and the localizer, no toast service) and parameters (lines 25-62). `CardTemplate` is an `[EditorRequired]` `RenderFragment<TItem>` (line 27); `CardActionsTemplate` is the optional `RenderFragment<TItem>?` for per-card controls (line 37). `FetchPageResult` (line 47), also `[EditorRequired]`, is the fetch delegate in the shape every Result-returning UI service already has, `(page, pageSize, cancellationToken)` returning `Result<(IReadOnlyList<TItem> Items, int TotalItems)>`, which is [`IEntityService<TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>`](#ientityservicetentitydto-tidentifiertype)`.GetPagedAsync` minus the filter and sort arguments. `PageSize` defaults to 10 (line 49), `EmptyIcon` to `SearchOff` (line 55), `MaxRenderedItems` to 500 (line 62).
  - State (lines 64-94): `_items`, `_totalCount`, `_currentPage`, `_generation`, the four render flags (`_isInitialLoad`, `_isLoadingMore`, `_hasMore`, `_loadError`), `_loadErrorMessage`, the interop handles (`_sentinelRef`, `_observer`, the shared [`InfiniteScrollObserver<TOwner>`](#infinitescrollobservertowner) that owns the module, the `DotNetObjectReference` and the observer id, and `_cts`), `_reobservePending` (line 93) and `_disposed`.
  - `OnInitializedAsync` (lines 96-102) validates the delegate then loads page 1. `ValidateFetchParameter` (lines 109-116) throws an `InvalidOperationException` when `FetchPageResult` is null, deliberately *before* the load, so a misconfigured call site fails loudly instead of rendering as a load failure with a Retry button that can never succeed (lines 104-108).
  - `OnAfterRenderAsync` (lines 118-128) consumes and clears `_reobservePending` (lines 120-121), then attaches the observer only while more pages exist, there are items to scroll past and the initial load is done, either when none is observing yet (`_observer?.IsObserving != true`) or when a re-observe was queued (line 123). It lazily creates the shared [`InfiniteScrollObserver<TOwner>`](#infinitescrollobservertowner) (line 125) and calls `ObserveAsync(_sentinelRef)` (line 126); the helper tolerates `JSDisconnectedException` and `JSException` on both paths.
  - `OnSentinelVisible()` (lines 130-143), the `[JSInvokable]` entry point, returns a completed task when already loading, exhausted or disposed (lines 133-136), otherwise the `InvokeAsync` task that loads on the renderer's context and re-renders (lines 138-142).
  - `LoadNextPageAsync(bool isInitial)` (lines 145-237) is the core. It guards re-entry (lines 147-150), sets `_isLoadingMore` and clears the error state (lines 152-154), and, for a next-page load only, queues a render at once so the "Loading more items" status paints while the fetch is in flight, because a load started from a JS callback or the Retry button otherwise renders nothing until it ends (lines 156-162). It then snapshots the generation and publishes a fresh `CancellationTokenSource` (lines 164-168), computes `targetPage` (line 173), and awaits the delegate (line 177). After the await it checks disposal and generation (line 182), unwraps the `Result` with `TryGetValue` and routes a failure to `SetLoadFailed` (lines 187-193), and only then commits: advance the page (line 197), append the items through `AppendNew` and keep the count of new rows (line 199), record the total (line 200), set `_hasMore` from `HasMoreAfter(appended)` (line 201), which is where the DOM cap and the empty-append guard stop the loop, and call `MarkReobserveAfterAppend(isInitial)` (line 203). `OperationCanceledException` is swallowed as a normal supersession (lines 205-208); any other exception, caught under a scoped `CA1031` suppression, raises the generic failure, again only for the current generation (lines 209-219). The `finally` (lines 220-236) is careful about ownership: only the current generation may clear `_isLoadingMore` (a superseding reset already cleared it and may have set it again), and only the still-current `CancellationTokenSource` is disposed here (`ReferenceEquals`, line 229), because a resetter that took one over already cancelled and disposed it.
  - `AppendNew(IEnumerable<TItem> items)` (lines 245-253) appends only the rows not already shown and returns how many were new. Offset paging plus an insert ahead of the window can repeat a row across pages, and rows are keyed by value (`@key="item"`), so a repeat would be two siblings with one key and a render error (lines 239-244). It filters lazily with `_items.Contains` while adding (line 250), so a row repeated inside the same page is caught too; records compare by value, the same equality `@key` uses. `HasMoreAfter(int appended)` (lines 261-262) is `appended > 0 && _items.Count < _totalCount && _items.Count < MaxRenderedItems`: besides the rendered-item cap it stops when a page added nothing new (an empty page, or a window shifted by a whole page), so the re-observed sentinel cannot re-request the same page forever; `ResetAsync` starts over (lines 255-260).
  - `MarkReobserveAfterAppend(bool isInitial)` (lines 268-274) sets `_reobservePending` after a non-initial append that left more pages. The IntersectionObserver reports threshold crossings only, so a sentinel still inside the viewport after the append would never fire again; re-observing creates a fresh observer, which delivers an initial entry with the current state (lines 90-92). This is the same stall [`InfiniteScrollSentinel`](#infinitescrollsentinel) guards against with its post-load re-attach.
  - `SetLoadFailed(Result? failure)` (lines 286-290) sets the inline error state and nothing else: no toast is raised, because the inline alert is announced on its own, rendered in place of the list for a failed first page or below it for a later page (lines 276-279). The message comes from `failure?.LocalizedErrorMessage(L)` (line 289); a raw exception passes `null`, because exception text is neither translatable nor safe to surface (lines 280-284), and the generic resource string is used instead.
  - `CardCallback(TItem item)` (lines 299-302) binds one row's click behavior for the markup below. When `OnCardClick` has a delegate it returns an `EventCallback.Factory.Create` wrapping the invoke; when it does not, it returns `default`, deliberately not `EventCallback.Empty`, because `EventCallback.Empty` wraps a no-op `Action` so its `HasDelegate` is still true and every card would present as interactive. `default` is the only value `ClickableCard` reads as "no handler wired", which is what lets it render a plain, non-focusable card instead of a keyboard control that does nothing (lines 292-298).
  - `CardActions(TItem item)` (line 308) binds one row to `CardActionsTemplate`, or returns `null` when the consumer supplied none, which keeps `ClickableCard` on its original one-element markup (lines 304-307). `RetryAsync` (line 310) is a plain `LoadNextPageAsync(isInitial: false)`; the load queues its own render.
  - `ResetAsync()` (lines 316-354) is the public API a page calls when filters change. Order matters and is commented: bump the generation *first* so any in-flight fetch is already superseded (line 320), then cancel and dispose the stale token source (lines 322-329), then clear `_isLoadingMore` explicitly (lines 331-334, because the superseded load will not clear it), then reset the list and every flag (lines 336-342), detach the observer (lines 344-347), and reload from page 1 (lines 349-353).
  - `DisposeAsync` (lines 356-377) guards re-entry, cancels and disposes the token source (lines 367-371), then delegates to `_observer.DisposeAsync()` (lines 373-376), which detaches the observer, releases the JS module and disposes the `DotNetObjectReference`.
  - The markup (`Components/Lists/MobileInfiniteScrollList.razor:1-64`) renders one of four shapes: an indeterminate progress bar inside a `role="status"` live region on the initial load (lines 5-14), the load-failure alert when the first page itself failed (lines 15-20, because a failed first page is not an empty list), `EmptyState` when the list came back empty (lines 21-24), or a `MudStack` of `ClickableCard` wrappers around the caller's template, each keyed by item and wired to `CardCallback(item)` and `CardActions(item)` (lines 27-34). Below the cards it renders the sentinel `div` only while `_hasMore`, with a polite live-region spinner while a page loads (lines 36-49), and the same alert when a later page failed (lines 51-54). That alert is one `RenderFragment`, `LoadFailedAlert`, carrying `role="alert"` with the message and a Retry button (lines 58-63).
- **Why it's built this way**: the component encapsulates the part of infinite scroll that is genuinely hard to get right (supersession, cancellation ownership, disposal, the DOM cap) and leaves the part that is app-specific (what a card looks like, where the data comes from) to parameters. The `Result`-returning delegate rather than a raw `Task<List<T>>` is what makes a *localized* failure message reachable without the component knowing any error catalogue.
- **Where it's used**: the mobile branch of every page built on [`ListPageShell<TItem>`](#listpageshelltitem), which renders it at `Components/Lists/ListPageShell.razor:36` (the ADC conference admin lists such as `SessionList.razor`, `SpeakerList.razor` and `RoomList.razor`, and Store's `CategoryList.razor`, `ProductList.razor` and `ShoppingCartList.razor`). Pages that render it directly: ADC's `PublicEventList.razor:25`, `PublicSessionListView.razor:6` and the check-in `AttendeeSearchPanel.razor:28`, and Store's `MMCA.Store/Source/Modules/Sales/MMCA.Store.Sales.UI/Pages/Orders/OrderList.razor:39`. Covered by [`MobileInfiniteScrollListTests`](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup). The list-shell placement is recorded in ADR-146 (`Website/docs-src/adr/146-ui-page-bases-and-list-shell.md`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: `MaxRenderedItems` bounds the DOM but there is no virtualization, so 500 rendered cards remain in the DOM; whether that is acceptable on a given device is not determinable from source. A consumer fetch delegate that ignores its `CancellationToken` still runs to completion after a reset: the generation guard discards its results, but the request itself is not stopped.

### MultiFactorRequiredListener

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Components.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Auth/MultiFactorRequiredListener.cs:24` · Level 3 · class (internal sealed component)

- **What it is**: a markup-less layout component that sends the user to the two-factor page when the
  API refuses a request because the session lacks a second factor. [TwoFactorUIModule](#twofactoruimodule)
  contributes it to the layout through `LayoutComponentTypes` (`TwoFactorUIModule.cs:28`), so a host
  that opts into two-factor gets the redirect with no page changes (ADR-067,
  `Website/docs-src/adr/067-ui-module-shell-composition.md`).
- **Depends on**: `ComponentBase` and `IDisposable` (`MultiFactorRequiredListener.cs:24`),
  [ITokenStorageService](#itokenstorageservice) (`:28`), `NavigationManager` (`:30`),
  [MultiFactorRequiredSignal](#multifactorrequiredsignal) for the subscription (`:41`),
  [ReturnUrlProtector](#returnurlprotector) (`:81`) and `TwoFactorUIModule.AccountPath` (`:47`, `:83`).
- **Concept introduced, a step-up redirect that cannot become an open redirect or a loop.**
  `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether a second-factor requirement is enforced consistently and
  whether a return URL can be abused. The listener sanitizes the current location through
  `ReturnUrlProtector.Sanitize` with `/` as the fallback before putting it in `returnUrl` (`:81-83`), and
  never redirects away from the two-factor page or the sign-in page (`IsExempt`, `:46-48`), so the
  refusal that brought the user there cannot bounce them again.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `OnInitialized` (`:40-41`) subscribes through `MultiFactorRequiredSignal.Subscribe(TokenStorage, OnRequired)`;
    `Dispose` (`:33-37`) disposes and clears the subscription.
  - `OnRequired` (`:50`) discards `RedirectAsync`, which dispatches `Redirect` through `InvokeAsync`
    and swallows `ObjectDisposedException` and `InvalidOperationException`, the two shapes of a circuit
    that ended between the refusal and the dispatch (`:52-66`).
  - `Redirect` (`:68-84`) does nothing outside an interactive renderer (`:70-73`), reads the
    base-relative path (`:75`), returns for an exempt path (`:76-79`), and navigates to
    `{AccountPath}?required=true&returnUrl=...` with the escaped, sanitized path (`:81-83`).
  - `IsExempt` (`:46-48`) is an ordinal, case-insensitive prefix match on the trimmed `AccountPath` and
    on `login`.
- **Why it's built this way**: listening at the layout rather than in each page means every refused call,
  whichever page made it, takes the user to the same place, and the internal visibility keeps it a
  detail of the two-factor module rather than a component consumers place by hand.
- **Where it's used**: registered by `TwoFactorUIModule`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/TwoFactor/TwoFactorUIModule.cs:28`); pinned by
  `MultiFactorRequiredListenerTests`
  (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Components/Auth/MultiFactorRequiredListenerTests.cs`),
  `TwoFactorOptInRenderTests` and `TwoFactorUIModuleTests`.

### ChangePasswordCard

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Components.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Auth/ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:23` · Level 4 · class (partial component)

- **What it is**: the shared change-password form for a signed-in user: three password fields inside a
  `MudForm`, client-side length and confirmation checks, and a submit that calls the auth service and
  reports the outcome through toasts. A consumer app drops it into its profile page instead of
  re-implementing the form (ADC does so with a bare `<ChangePasswordCard />`,
  `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.UI/Pages/Users/Profile/Profile.razor:83`).
- **Depends on**: [IAuthUIService](#iauthuiservice) (`@inject AuthService`,
  `ChangePasswordCard.razor:2`), [IToastService](#itoastservice) (`ChangePasswordCard.razor:3`),
  `IStringLocalizer<ChangePasswordCard>` (`ChangePasswordCard.razor:4`) with the plural helper
  [StringLocalizerPluralExtensions](#stringlocalizerpluralextensions), [ResultUiExtensions](#resultuiextensions)
  for `LocalizedErrorMessage` (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:165`),
  [ComponentLifetimeExtensions](#componentlifetimeextensions) for `LifetimeToken()`
  (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:149`), [PasswordComplexity](group-08-auth.md#passwordcomplexity) and
  [ChangePasswordRequest](group-08-auth.md#changepasswordrequest) (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:30-31`,
  `:59`, `:120`), [AuthFieldMessages](#authfieldmessages) for the complexity message
  (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:122`), and the nested [FieldRefusal](#fieldrefusal) (`:43-44`).
  Externals: `MudForm` and `MudTextField` from MudBlazor.
- **Concept introduced, a form that reports the server's reason, not its own guess.**
  `[Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]` assesses whether validation feedback is honest and
  where it is raised. Two layers are visible here. The client checks only what it can know cheaply:
  the new password meets `MinLength` (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:113-116`), satisfies the shared
  `PasswordComplexity` rule the server's strong-password rules also evaluate (`:118-122`), and the
  confirmation matches (`:125-128`); the server still enforces its own rules (doc comment,
  `ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:46-49`). A server refusal is shown with the server's own message when it
  has one, falling back to a fixed `ChangePassword.Failed` text only when the failure carries none
  (comment `ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:162-165`). When the refusal names the current or the new
  password field, it is also shown under that field via [FieldRefusal](#fieldrefusal)
  (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:166`, `:180-192`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - Parameters: `MinLength` defaults to `8`, the framework's password policy minimum, and also feeds the
    helper text (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:51`; `ChangePasswordCard.razor:18`). `MaxLength` is an
    `int?` that defaults to `PasswordComplexity.MaximumLength`, the bound the server's password
    rules enforce; `null` leaves the field unbounded (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:53-59`); the
    razor falls back to the private `NoMaxLength` constant `524288`, MudTextField's own default
    (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:25-26`; `ChangePasswordCard.razor:20`). `AdditionalActions`
    (`RenderFragment?`) renders extra actions, such as a device-management link, after the submit
    button (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:66`; `ChangePasswordCard.razor:38`).
  - Callbacks: `OnChanged` fires after success, once the toast has been shown
    (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:70`); `OnFailed` carries the failed `Result` after the failure
    toast, and is not raised for a client-side validation failure, which the form itself reports
    (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:77`).
  - Validators: all three return `null` for valid or empty input and leave the `Required` check to
    report a missing value (comment `ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:100-102`). `ValidateCurrentPassword`
    (`:103`) only echoes a server message held for the exact value still in the field.
    `ValidateNewPassword` (`:106`) checks length first, plural-aware through `L.Plural` (`:115`), then
    `PasswordComplexity.Evaluate`: a failing value gets `AuthFieldMessages.PasswordComplexity` (`:122`),
    a passing one gets any held server message (`:121`). The mismatch uses
    `Validation.PasswordsDoNotMatch` (`:128`), and the confirmation comparison is ordinal (`:126`).
  - `SavePasswordAsync` (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:130`) opens with a re-entrancy guard before the first
    await: it returns when the `@ref`-set form is absent or a save is already running (`:135`), because a
    second click before the disabled render would resend the stale current password, which the server
    refuses and counts toward lockout (comment `:132-134`). It then sets `_isSaving` (`:140`) and,
    inside the `try`, validates the form and stops on invalid (`:143-147`) before calling
    `AuthService.ChangePasswordAsync(current, new, _cts.LifetimeToken())` (`:149`). On success it resets
    the form, clears the three fields, toasts `ChangePassword.Success` and raises `OnChanged`
    (`:151-158`). On failure it toasts (`:165`), calls `ShowFieldRefusalsAsync` (`:166`) and raises
    `OnFailed(result)` (`:167`). A cancelled call is swallowed (`:170-173`), and `_isSaving` always
    clears in `finally` (`:176`).
  - `ShowFieldRefusalsAsync` (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:183`) builds a [FieldRefusal](#fieldrefusal)
    for the current-password field (matching the wrong-password code `Auth.InvalidCurrentPassword`,
    `:32`) and for the new-password field, then re-validates the form so the message lands under the
    field and in the summary (`:185-191`).
  - Disposal: the component implements `IDisposable` (`ChangePasswordCard.razor:5`).
    `Dispose(bool)` is idempotent, sets `_disposed`, then cancels and disposes the
    `CancellationTokenSource` (`ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:88-98`). The `MudForm` reference is not
    disposed here because the renderer owns it (comment `ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:36`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the cancel-on-dispose token is what makes a navigation away, or an
  InteractiveAuto render-mode transition, harmless: the in-flight request is cancelled and the
  `OperationCanceledException` is expected (comment `ChangePasswordCard.razor.cs:172`). Taking
  `MinLength` and `MaxLength` as parameters lets a consumer tighten the form without forking it, while
  the server remains the authority. Localization follows ADR-027
  (`Website/docs-src/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.md`).
- **Where it's used**: ADC's profile page renders it (`Profile.razor:83`), and [PasskeysPanel](#passkeyspanel)
  mirrors its card layout (`Profile.razor:106`). Its behavior is pinned by
  `ChangePasswordCardTests`
  (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Components/Auth/ChangePasswordCardTests.cs`) and
  `ChangePasswordCardErrorSummaryTests`, and
  `FormsConventionTestsBase` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Hosting/MMCA.Common.Testing.Architecture/Bases/Ui/FormsConventionTestsBase.cs:33`)
  references it by its `<ChangePasswordCard` tag.

### ListPageShell<TItem>

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Components.Lists` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Lists/ListPageShell.razor.cs:23` · Level 4 · class (generic partial component)

- **What it is**: the shared chrome of an admin list page: a `PageHeader` with a cancel-loading button

  [DataGridListPageBase<TDto>](#datagridlistpagebasetdto) supplies the data callbacks, the columns and

- **Depends on**: [MobileInfiniteScrollList<TItem>](#mobileinfinitescrolllisttitem) for the phone branch
  (`ListPageShell.razor:36`; `ListPageShell.razor.cs:144`), MudBlazor's `MudDataGrid<TItem>` and

  copied. Every list page passes the same parameters into one shell, so a change to the header, the
  search row, the empty state or the pager reaches every list at once. `[Rubric §21, Accessibility]`

  - States: `LoadFailed`, `EmptyConfirmed` and `EmptyMessage` (`:123-129`), `OnRetry` (`:132`),

### PasskeySignInButton

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Components.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Auth/PasskeySignInButton.razor.cs:25` · Level 4 · class (partial component)

- **What it is**: the sign-in page's passkey entry point (the opt-in passkey sign-in of ADR-139,
  `Website/docs-src/adr/139-passkeys-webauthn-opt-in-sign-in.md`). It offers a "sign in with a passkey"
  button and, where the browser supports it, starts passkey autofill so a saved passkey is suggested
  in the sign-in form without a click.
- **Depends on**: [IPasskeyUIService](#ipasskeyuiservice) for the server half of the ceremony
  (`PasskeySignInButton.razor.cs:40`), [IPasskeyCapability](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#ipasskeycapability)
  for the platform half (`:42`), [PasskeySignInRequest](group-08-auth.md#passkeysigninrequest) (`:133`),
  [ResultUiExtensions](#resultuiextensions) for `LocalizedErrorMessage` (`:145`),
  [SharedResource](#sharedresource) (`:44`) and [ComponentLifetimeExtensions](#componentlifetimeextensions)
  for `LifetimeToken()` (`:73`).
- **Concept introduced, no server challenge until the browser can use it.** `[Rubric §11, Security]`
  assesses whether an authentication ceremony issues only what it can redeem. Autofill checks
  `IsAutofillAvailableAsync` before asking the server for options, because the options store a server
  challenge that a browser without conditional mediation could never redeem (comment `:71-72`, `:73`).
  An explicit click cancels any running autofill first (`:104`) so the two ceremonies never overlap.
- **Walkthrough**
  - Parameters: `OnSignedIn` is raised once the passkey signed the user in and the tokens are stored
    (`:33-34`); `EnableAutofill` defaults to true (`:37-38`).
  - `OnAfterRenderAsync` (`:62-91`) runs on the first render only, when autofill is enabled and the
    component is not disposed (`:64`): it checks support (`:73`), begins a sign-in flow (`:78`) and on
    success starts autofill with a callback that completes the flow on the renderer's context
    (`:81-84`). An `OperationCanceledException` is swallowed only when disposed (`:87`).
  - `SignInAsync` (`:93-129`) guards on `_isBusy` (`:95`), clears the error, cancels autofill (`:104`),
    begins a flow (`:105`) and shows the failure message when that fails (`:106-110`), then asks the
    platform for an assertion (`:112`); a `null` credential shows the localized
    `Auth.Login.PasskeyCancelled` text (`:113-117`), otherwise it completes the flow (`:119`).
    `_isBusy` clears in `finally` (`:125-128`).
  - `CompleteAsync` (`:131-142`) posts a `PasskeySignInRequest(flowId, assertion)` (`:133`); a failure
    sets the message and re-renders (`:134-139`), a success raises `OnSignedIn` (`:141`).
  - `FailureMessage` (`:144-145`) prefers the result's localized message and falls back to
    `Auth.Login.PasskeyFailed`.
  - `DisposeAsync` (`:47-59`) is idempotent, cancels and disposes the token source and cancels any
    running autofill (`:57`).
- **Why it's built this way**: splitting the ceremony between a UI service (server) and a device
  capability (platform) lets the same button run in a browser and in a native head without a branch.
- **Where it's used**: the shared sign-in page
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Auth/Login.razor:170`).
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: no test file references the type by name outside its defining file; its
  coverage, if any, runs through the sign-in page.

### PasskeysPanel

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Components.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Auth/PasskeysPanel.razor.cs:21` · Level 4 · class (partial component)

- **What it is**: the signed-in user's passkey manager (ADR-139,
  `Website/docs-src/adr/139-passkeys-webauthn-opt-in-sign-in.md`): it lists the account's passkeys with
  their added and last-used dates, adds a new one with an optional name, renames one in place, and
  deletes one after a confirmation.
- **Depends on**: [IPasskeyUIService](#ipasskeyuiservice) (`PasskeysPanel.razor.cs:39`),
  [IPasskeyCapability](group-26-device-capability-layer.md#ipasskeycapability) (`:41`),
  [IAppDialogService](#iappdialogservice) (`:43`), [IToastService](#itoastservice) (`:45`),
  [ViewerTimeZone](#viewertimezone) (`:49`), `IStringLocalizer<PasskeysPanel>` (`:51`),
  [PasskeyResponse](group-08-auth.md#passkeyresponse) (`:27`), [PasskeyRegisterRequest](group-08-auth.md#passkeyregisterrequest)
  (`:129`), [ResultUiExtensions](#resultuiextensions) (`:241`) and
  [ComponentLifetimeExtensions](#componentlifetimeextensions) (`:74`).
- **Concept introduced, a refusal the user can fix gets its own words.** `[Rubric §24, Forms,
  Validation & UX Safety]` assesses whether an error tells the user what to do. Most refusals show the
  server's own reason (the last-passkey rule, a name that is too long; comment `:221-222`), but a
  step-up refusal, code `Passkeys.StepUpRequired` restated as `StepUpRequiredCode` because UI references
  Shared only (`:23-24`), shows the localized `Passkeys.SignInAgain` text instead, the one refusal with
  an action the user can take (`FailureMessage`, `:236-241`). `[Rubric §11, Security]` applies to the
  delete path: it asks for a destructive confirmation first (`:194-199`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - `OnInitializedAsync` (`:68`) calls `LoadAsync` (`:80-102`), which lists the passkeys (`:84`), toasts
    a failure (`:91`) and clears `_isLoading` in `finally` (`:98-101`).
  - `OnAfterRenderAsync` (`:71-78`) resolves the viewer's time zone on first render, so the dates render
    as the viewer's local date rather than the UTC date (comment `:47-48`); `DescribeLastUsed`
    (`:243-246`) formats with the short `d` pattern (`:245`) or shows `Passkeys.NeverUsed`.
  - `AddAsync` (`:104-145`) begins registration (`:114`), asks the platform to create a credential
    (`:121`), toasts `Passkeys.AddCancelled` as info when the user backs out (`:122-126`), completes the
    registration with the trimmed name or `null` (`:128-130`), and clears the name field on success
    (`:132-135`).
  - Rename: `StartRename` and `CancelRename` hold the row being renamed and its draft (`:147-157`);
    `SaveRenameAsync` (`:159-185`) posts the new name (`:169`) and leaves edit mode on success.
  - `DeleteAsync` (`:187-219`) confirms through `Dialogs.ConfirmAsync(..., destructive: true)`
    (`:194-199`) before deleting (`:208`).
  - `AfterChangeAsync` (`:223-234`) toasts a failure, or toasts the success key, re-reads the list so the
    rows are the server's, and raises `OnChanged` (`:232-233`).
  - Every mutating method guards on `_isBusy` and swallows `OperationCanceledException` only when
    disposed; `DisposeAsync` (`:54-65`) is idempotent and cancels and disposes the token source.
- **Why it's built this way**: re-reading the list after every change, rather than patching the local
  copy, keeps the rows identical to what the server holds.
- **Where it's used**: ADC's profile page
  (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.UI/Pages/Users/Profile/Profile.razor:114`); pinned
  by `PasskeysPanelTests`
  (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Components/Auth/PasskeysPanelTests.cs`) and ADC's
  `ProfilePasskeysTests`.

### ClientConfigUiSections

> MMCA.Common.UI.Web · `MMCA.Common.UI.Web.ClientConfig` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/ClientConfig/ClientConfigUiSections.cs:34` · Level 1 · class (internal static)

- **What it is**: the helper that copies Common.UI's own `Layout`, `Registration`, `SignIn` and
  `Legal` settings from the server head's configuration into the anonymous `/client-config` document,
  so a value set where production values are set (an environment variable, Key Vault,
  `appsettings.Production.json` on the UI container) renders the same after WebAssembly hydration as
  in the prerender, with no second copy in the WebAssembly bundle (class summary,
  `ClientConfigUiSections.cs:8-13`).
- **Depends on**: [LayoutSettings](#layoutsettings), [RegistrationSettings](#registrationsettings),
  [SignInSettings](#signinsettings) and [LegalSettings](#legalsettings) (each one's `SectionName` and
  type, `ClientConfigUiSections.cs:39-42`). Externals: `Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration`
  (`IConfiguration`, binder `Get(Type)`), `System.Text.Json` (`JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase`) and
  `System.Reflection` (`PropertyInfo`, `BindingFlags`).
- **Concept introduced, forward only what the settings class declares and what the server sets.**
  `[Rubric §26, Front-End Security]` assesses what reaches the browser. The remarks
  (`ClientConfigUiSections.cs:14-33`) give two rules. Each section is bound to its Common.UI settings
  type and only that type's settable properties are written, so an unrelated or secret key that
  happens to sit under the same section name in the server configuration never reaches the anonymous
  document; every forwarded value is already rendered on public pages. And a section absent from the
  server configuration, or a property whose key is absent, is skipped, so the WebAssembly client's own
  defaults hold for everything the server leaves unset. `[Rubric §20, Design System & Theming]` applies
  because `Layout` (brand, footer) is one of the forwarded sections, so the theme a head configures
  survives hydration.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `Forwarded` (`ClientConfigUiSections.cs:37-43`) is the fixed list of `(SectionName, SettingsType)`
    pairs, in the order they are written.
  - `Build(IConfiguration)` (`ClientConfigUiSections.cs:51`) loops the list (`:53`), skips a section
    that does not exist (`:55-59`) or binds to `null` (`:61-65`), then builds a dictionary keyed by the
    camelCased property name over the declared settable properties whose key is present in that
    section (`section.GetSection(property.Name).Value is not null`, `:67-72`), reading each value from
    the bound instance so the binder's type conversion applies. A section with no present key yields
    nothing; otherwise it yields the camelCased section name and the map (`:74-77`).
  - `DeclaredSettableProperties(Type)` (`ClientConfigUiSections.cs:88-91`) keeps public instance
    properties with a public setter or init accessor and no index parameters, which is what
    configuration binding writes; computed members such as `LegalSettings.HasFooterLinks` are excluded
    (doc `:81-87`). It is `internal` so the tests can reach it.
- **Why it's built this way**: forwarding from the server's bound configuration means one place sets a
  production value; binding then reading back through the settings type keeps the document to the
  public shape the class declares. The host's extras win: a head that still adds one of these
  sections through its `ClientConfig` callback replaces the forwarded copy (remarks `:28-32`), because
  [ClientConfigEndpointExtensions](#clientconfigendpointextensions) writes these sections before the
  extras.
- **Where it's used**: called once per request by
  [ClientConfigEndpointExtensions](#clientconfigendpointextensions)`.MapClientConfigEndpoint`
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/ClientConfig/ClientConfigEndpointExtensions.cs:104-107`);
  pinned by `ClientConfigEndpointTests`
  (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Tests/ClientConfig/ClientConfigEndpointTests.cs`).

### AuthenticatedServiceBase

> MMCA.Common.UI · `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Api` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:17` · Level 2 · class (abstract)

- **What it is**: the base class every UI-side HTTP service inherits. It supplies one shared Polly
  retry policy, two ways to get an `HttpClient` with a bearer token already attached, and the
  idempotency-key generator that makes those retries safe.
- **Depends on**: [ITokenStorageService](#itokenstorageservice), imported from the token namespace
  `MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Auth.Tokens` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:5`); its documentation also
  names [AuthDelegatingHandler](#authdelegatinghandler) as the thing it deliberately bypasses and
  `Auth.Tokens.ITokenRefresher`, that is [ITokenRefresher](#itokenrefresher), as the source of the
  replay token. From `MMCA.Common.Shared.Resilience` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:4`) it reads
  [RetryAfterHeader](group-16-aspire-orchestration.md#retryafterheader) and the
  `MaxRetryAfterWait` ceiling on
  [HttpResilienceDefaults](group-16-aspire-orchestration.md#httpresiliencedefaults). It also tests its
  storage for [ISessionAwareTokenStorage](#isessionawaretokenstorage)
  (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:102`), tells [AuthDelegatingHandler](#authdelegatinghandler) which
  storage a bearer came from (`AuthDelegatingHandler.TrackTokenOwner`, `AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:84`),
  and reads the header name from [IdempotencyHeaders](group-08-auth.md#idempotencyheaders)
  (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:200`). Externals: `IHttpClientFactory`, `TimeProvider`, `Polly` and
  `Polly.Retry`.
- **Concept introduced, why a base class and not just the handler pipeline.**
  `[Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]` assesses whether transient failures are absorbed
  rather than surfaced; the retry policy is that. The sharper teaching is in the
  `CreateAuthenticatedClientAsync` doc comment (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:63-68`):
  `IHttpClientFactory` creates its handlers in a separate DI scope from the Blazor circuit, so a
  `DelegatingHandler` cannot reach the circuit's `IJSRuntime` to read the in-memory access token. The
  base class works around that by reading the token from the circuit-scoped storage service itself and
  setting the header directly. `[Rubric §9, API & Contract Design]` covers the idempotency half:
  retrying a POST is only safe if the server can recognize the repeat, which is what
  [ADR-017](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/017-request-idempotency.html) provides.
- **Walkthrough**
  - `RetryPolicy` is a `protected static readonly AsyncRetryPolicy<HttpResponseMessage>` built once from
    the shipped backoff (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:37`), so one policy instance serves the whole app
    rather than one per service instance per circuit. `ApiClientName` pins the named client to
    `"APIClient"` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:39`), and both constructor arguments are null-checked
    into private fields (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:41-42`).
  - `SharedRetryPolicy` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:48`) is an `internal static` getter that returns
    that same `RetryPolicy` instance. Its doc comment (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:44-47`) names the
    only reader, [IdempotentReadRetry](#idempotentreadretry), which reuses the exact policy object
    without inheriting from this class, so the anonymous read path and the authenticated one cannot
    drift apart.
  - `NewIdempotencyKey()` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:61`) returns a compact
    `Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")`, and its remarks (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:53-59`) carry the
    load-bearing rule: the value is generated once per logical operation and reused across every retry
    attempt, because the server-side idempotency filter keys its cached response off it. Generating a
    new key per attempt would defeat the dedup entirely and let a retry create a duplicate record.
  - `CreateAuthenticatedClientAsync()` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:69`) resolves the `"APIClient"`
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:71`), reads the token (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:75`), sets
    `Authorization: Bearer` when non-blank (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:76-85`), and catches
    `InvalidOperationException` to proceed without a token during SSR prerender, when JS interop is
    unavailable (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:87-90`). When it attaches a bearer it also calls
    `AuthDelegatingHandler.TrackTokenOwner(token, _tokenStorageService)`
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:84`): the handler in the client's pipeline holds a different storage
    instance (its own DI scope), so it is told which instance the bearer came from, and a 401 to it
    reaches the storage the component's auth state listens to (comment, `:81-83`).
  - `StorageRenewsRejectedTokens` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:102`) is a `private protected` flag that
    is true when the storage is an [ISessionAwareTokenStorage](#isessionawaretokenstorage). Its doc
    comment (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:95-101`) states the contract: such storage has already had the
    ONE renewal a 401 earns made on it by [AuthDelegatingHandler](#authdelegatinghandler) before the 401
    reaches the caller, so a caller replaying the request reads the renewed token instead of refreshing
    a second time. `ReadRenewedAccessTokenAsync(string? rejectedToken)` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:113`)
    is that read: it returns `null` when no bearer was sent (`:115-118`), and otherwise re-reads storage
    (`:120`) and returns the value only when it is non-blank and differs ordinally from the refused token
    (`:121-123`), so a session the renewal ended, or a storage still holding the refused token, yields
    nothing to replay with.
  - `CreateClientWithToken(string accessToken)` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:134`) is the replay path.
    Its doc comment (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:126-132`) explains why it exists: after the API answers
    `401`, the stored token still looks fresh by the client clock, so re-reading storage would just
    resend the token the server has already rejected. The caller passes the token it acquired straight
    from [ITokenRefresher](#itokenrefresher); the method rejects a blank one
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:136`) and stamps the header unconditionally
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:139`).
  - `IsRetryableResponse(HttpResponseMessage, TimeProvider)` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:157`) is
    the retry predicate. It first excludes `501 Not Implemented` and `505 HTTP Version Not Supported`
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:159-162`) because, as the remarks say
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:148-156`), those are permanent verdicts and retrying only burns the
    budget and delays the error the caller needs to see. It next refuses any response for which
    `RetryAfterHeader.ExceedsRetryBudget` is true (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:164-167`;
    `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Shared/Resilience/RetryAfterHeader.cs:75`): a 429 whose
    `Retry-After` asks for longer than `HttpResilienceDefaults.MaxRetryAfterWait`, 8 seconds
    (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Shared/Resilience/HttpResilienceDefaults.cs:40`), means the
    rate-limit window will not reset within any wait worth holding the user for, so the refusal
    surfaces at once. It then asks `IsReplaySafe` whether the request may be sent again and gives up if not
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:169-172`). Only then does it accept anything `>= 500` plus
    `408 Request Timeout` and `429 Too Many Requests` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:174-175`), the two
    codes where the server is explicitly inviting a later attempt.
  - `IsReplaySafe(HttpRequestMessage? request)` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:188`) is the gate that
    keeps a retry from duplicating a write. Its doc comment (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:178-185`)
    states the rule: GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE and the other idempotent verbs are always safe to re-send,
    while a POST or PATCH is safe only when it carries a non-blank `Idempotency-Key` header, which an
    `[Idempotent]` endpoint deduplicates on. Without a key, a failed attempt may still have run
    server-side, and a retry can hit a rate limit and replace the server's real failure with a 429. A
    response with no request attached is treated as safe (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:190-193`). The
    method is `internal static` so a test can pin it directly, and the doc comment on `RetryPolicy`
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:21-36`) carries the same POST/PATCH caveat.
  - The exception arm of the policy sees no response, so it learns replay safety another way.
    `MarkReplaySafety(HttpRequestException, HttpRequestMessage)` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:221`)
    stores `IsReplaySafe(request)` in `exception.Data` under the `internal const ReplaySafeDataKey`
    (`:210`); [AuthDelegatingHandler](#authdelegatinghandler), the outermost handler `AddUIShared` adds to
    the API client, calls it (doc comment `:212-220`, which notes that on a host calling
    `AddServiceDefaults` the service-discovery handler wraps it, and so does the standard resilience
    handler unless the host removes it, as `AddMmcaBlazorWebHost` does). `IsRetryableException` (`:232`)
    then retries a transport failure unless it was marked not replay-safe (a POST or PATCH without an
    `Idempotency-Key`) AND failed after the request may have been sent: only `NameResolutionError`,
    `ConnectionError` and `SecureConnectionError` (failures before send, the rule the gRPC client
    applies) still retry (`:233-236`, doc `:224-231`). An unmarked exception keeps the retry
    (`Data[...] is not false`, `:233`).
  - `DefaultBackoff(int attempt)` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:246-248`) is the shipped schedule:
    `500 * 2^(attempt - 1)` milliseconds (0.5s, 1s, 2s for retries 1, 2 and 3) plus up to 250 ms of
    random jitter, so a fleet of clients does not re-converge on the same instant. It is `internal` so a
    test can pin the schedule (doc `:240-245`). The `RetryPolicy` doc comment
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:21-36`) explains why the schedule is short: a read that fails fast
    spends at most about 4.25 seconds waiting between attempts before it surfaces, a backend that
    accepts the request and then hangs is cut off by the client's own timeout instead
    (`HttpResilienceDefaults.TotalRequestTimeout`, which the comment gives as 90 seconds, set where the
    API client is registered) and that cancellation is not retried, and a 429 that names a
    `Retry-After` is outside the 4.25-second bound because each such retry can wait up to the cap. The
    `CA5394` suppression around it (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:238`) documents that the randomness
    only spaces retries and feeds no security decision.
  - `RetryDelay(int attempt, HttpResponseMessage? response, Func<int, TimeSpan> backoff, TimeProvider
    timeProvider)` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:261-269`, doc `:202-211`) picks the wait before each
    retry. For a `429 Too Many Requests` whose `Retry-After` parses through
    `RetryAfterHeader.TryGetDelay`
    (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Shared/Resilience/RetryAfterHeader.cs:43`) it waits exactly
    the named delay; everything else, including a 5xx and a transport failure with no response, keeps
    the backoff. The predicate has already refused a 429 over `MaxRetryAfterWait`, so the delay used
    here is bounded. The `TimeProvider` is the clock a date-form `Retry-After` is measured against.
  - `BuildRetryPolicy(Func<int, TimeSpan> backoff, TimeProvider? timeProvider = null)`
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:288-304`) is `internal` and backoff- and clock-injectable so a test
    can exercise the disposal and `Retry-After` contracts without waiting out the real delays; a null
    clock falls back to `TimeProvider.System` (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:292`). It retries 3 times
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:296-297`), with `sleepDurationProvider` routed through `RetryDelay`
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:298`). Its `onRetryAsync` disposes the retried attempt's response
    (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:299-303`); the remarks (`AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:275-282`) explain
    that Polly hands the caller only the final outcome (the policy handles `HttpRequestException` through
    `IsRetryableException`, `:294`, and responses through `IsRetryableResponse`, `:295`), so without
    this every intermediate 5xx, 408 or
    429 response leaks its content buffer and keeps its connection out of the handler pool until
    finalization, exactly under the sustained backend failure the retries exist to survive. A retried
    `HttpRequestException` carries no result, hence the null-conditional, and the final response is not
    disposed here because the caller owns it.
- **Why it's built this way**: the DI scope mismatch is a real Blazor Server constraint, not a
  preference, so the workaround has to live somewhere every service shares. The retry ceiling and
  jitter line up with the resilience posture in
  [ADR-009](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/009-resilience-and-recovery-objectives.html).
- **Where it's used**: inherited by
  [EntityServiceBase<TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>](#entityservicebasetentitydto-tidentifiertype)
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/EntityServiceBase.cs:38`),
  [ChildEntityServiceBase](#childentityservicebase)
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/ChildEntityServiceBase.cs:21`),
  [AuditHistoryService](#audithistoryservice)
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Auditing/AuditHistoryService.cs:24`) and
  [NotificationInboxService](#notificationinboxservice)
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Notifications/NotificationInboxService.cs:34`),
  and through them by every module-level UI service in the consumer apps. The members show up as
  `NewIdempotencyKey()` on creates and updates (`EntityServiceBase.cs:158` and
  `EntityServiceBase.cs:182`), `RetryPolicy.ExecuteAsync` around each
  call (`EntityServiceBase.cs:285` and `EntityServiceBase.cs:313`) and `CreateClientWithToken` on the
  401 replay (`NotificationInboxService.cs:154`). The policy itself is also reached without
  inheritance by [IdempotentReadRetry](#idempotentreadretry)
  (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/IdempotentReadRetry.cs:24`), which
  gives anonymous lookup services the same retries on GETs.
